questions.questionText: Amen Hospital wants to use surgery management system. This system will helps to the Doctor by identifying the surgery activities based on the pre-stored information and give appropriate message immediately when the doctor miss any activity related to surgery. According to the above case study, The software developer team must be given more emphasize which types of software quality requirements?
questions.explanation: In a critical system like surgery management, reliability is paramount to ensure the system consistently identifies missed activities and provides accurate messages, preventing potential harm.

questions.questionText: Amen Hospital wants to use surgery management system. This system will helps to the Doctor by identifying the surgery activities based on the pre-stored information and give appropriate message immediately when the doctor miss any activity related to surgery. According to the above case study, What types of software process model is using more fit with the system requirement?
questions.explanation: The Spiral model is suitable for systems with high risk, like medical applications, as it incorporates risk analysis and iterative development to ensure reliability.

questions.questionText: Ethiopian Airline Company is decided to use automated human resource management system. Assume you are working in Alsam Software Development Company (ASDC). ASDC agrees with the Ethiopian Airline Company to develop this system. The Ethiopian Airline Company administrator says that “the implementation language must be Csharp” but the software developer team want to implement the system by java programming language. Answer question number 3 and 4 based on the above case study. What types of requirement asked by Ethiopian Airline Company Administrator?
questions.explanation: Specifying the implementation language is a pseudo requirement, as it constrains how the system is built rather than what it does or its quality attributes.

questions.questionText: Ethiopian Airline Company is decided to use automated human resource management system. Assume you are working in Alsam Software Development Company (ASDC). ASDC agrees with the Ethiopian Airline Company to develop this system. The Ethiopian Airline Company administrator says that “the implementation language must be Csharp” but the software developer team want to implement the system by java programming language. Answer question number 3 and 4 based on the above case study. Assume you are project manager, what is your decision?
options: Accept the software development team idea and the system will be implementing by java.
Discuss with both Ethiopian airline administrator and software developer team to select common software programing language. If does not agree, the system development stop at early stage.
Decide to stop system development automatically.
According to software engineering rule, the software developer team idea has more acceptance than clients. Therefore, the system will be implementing by java.
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss with both Ethiopian airline administrator and software developer team to select common software programing language. If does not agree, the system development stop at early stage.
questions.explanation: As project manager, negotiating between client and team is key to resolve conflicts; if unresolved, stopping early avoids wasted effort.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following false about UML object model can be mapped to relational database during software design phase?
options: Each class is mapped to its own table
Each class attribute is mapped to a column in the table
Each class method is mapped to a relationship in the table
An instance of a class represents a row in the table
questions.correctAnswer: Each class method is mapped to a relationship in the table
questions.explanation: In mapping UML to relational databases, methods are not mapped to relationships; relationships represent associations between classes, while methods are behavior not directly mapped to database structures.

questions.questionText: Assume below two sentence are described non-functional requirements of Woldia university Student Information Management System (SIMS). What types of problem have been between those two non-functional requirement statements? “The system must work 24 hours per day, 7 days per week and 365 days per year” “The system can maintain within 3 hours”
questions.explanation: The two statements contradict each other: one requires constant availability, the other allows for maintenance downtime, leading to inconsistency in requirements.

questions.questionText: What is the correct HTML for creating a hyperlink?

questions.questionText: How can you open a link in a new tab/browser window?
questions.explanation: The target="_blank" attribute in the <a> tag opens the link in a new tab or window.

questions.questionText: In html, which attribute is used to specify that an input field must be filled out?
questions.explanation: The 'required' attribute in HTML5 ensures that the input field must be filled before submitting the form.

questions.questionText: What is the correct HTML for inserting an image:
questions.explanation: The tag uses 'src' for the image source and 'alt' for alternative text; it's self-closing.

questions.questionText: ________ is a metalanguage used to define new markup languages, and help you to create a language crafted specifically for your application or domain.
questions.explanation: XML is a metalanguage that allows users to define custom markup languages for specific purposes.

questions.questionText: _____________ are the software programs people use to consume the web?
questions.explanation: Web browsers are client-side software used to access and view web content.

questions.questionText: How do you create a cookie in PHP?
questions.explanation: The setcookie() function in PHP is used to set cookies.

questions.questionText: How do you create an array in PHP?
questions.explanation: Arrays in PHP are created using the array() function.

questions.questionText: What is MySQL?
options: Developed, distributed, and supported by Oracle Corporation
questions.explanation: MySQL is a relational DBMS, open-source, free, cross-platform, and supported by Oracle.

questions.questionText: Which statement is false?
options: When using the POST method, variables are displayed in the URL.
PHP can generate dynamic page content.
The if statement is used to execute some code only if a specified condition is true.
PHP scripts are executed on the server.
questions.correctAnswer: When using the POST method, variables are displayed in the URL.
questions.explanation: POST method sends data in the request body, not in the URL, unlike GET.

questions.questionText: Schema normalization is not for?
options: Reducing the number of tables in the schema.
Eliminating anomalies that could otherwise occur with inserts.
Eliminating anomalies that could otherwise occur with deletes.
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing the number of tables in the schema.
questions.explanation: Normalization typically increases the number of tables to reduce redundancy and anomalies.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is used to create a table?
questions.explanation: The standard SQL syntax for creating a table is CREATE TABLE table_name (column_name datatype);

questions.questionText: What is the difference between Generalization and Specialization?
options: Generalization and Specialization is like the Top-Down Approach
Generalization and Specialization is like the Bottom-Up Approach
Generalization is like a Bottom-Up approach and Specialization is like a Top-Down Approach
Generalization is like the Top-Down approach and Specialization is like the Bottom-Up Approach
questions.correctAnswer: Generalization is like a Bottom-Up approach and Specialization is like a Top-Down Approach
questions.explanation: Generalization combines specific entities into general ones (bottom-up), while specialization divides general entities into specific ones (top-down).

questions.questionText: A database language which provides users with high privilege command granting privileges and allowing granted privileges by the owner at any time is called ______?
questions.explanation: Data Control Language (DCL) includes commands like GRANT and REVOKE for managing privileges.

questions.questionText: A rule assigned to a column in a table that prevents certain types of inconsistency data value from being inserted or placed in the column?
questions.explanation: Constraints enforce rules on data in tables to maintain integrity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not Functions of Structured Query Language?
options: It can execute and retrieve queries against a database
It can insert and update records in a database
It can create stored procedures and views in a database
questions.explanation: SQL can do all these: SELECT for retrieve, INSERT/UPDATE for manipulation, CREATE for procedures and views. So 'not' is none, but answer key says D, meaning all are functions, so the 'not' is none of them is not a function.

questions.questionText: ______ is a set of one or more attributes taken collectively to uniquely identify a record?
questions.explanation: A super key is any set of attributes that uniquely identifies a record; candidate keys are minimal super keys.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of object based logical model?
questions.explanation: ER model is object-based, representing entities and relationships.

questions.questionText: Which of the following refers to the number of attributes in a relation?
questions.explanation: Degree is the number of attributes in a relation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is odd?
questions.explanation: Locking and Time Stamping are pessimistic concurrency control methods, while Optimistic is a different approach assuming no conflicts.

questions.questionText: Which level of security measures concerned with authorization of database users for access the content at different levels and privileges?
questions.explanation: Human level security involves user authentication and authorization for access control.

questions.questionText: What is a mechanism for enforcing limits on access to a resource in an environment where there are many threads of execution?
questions.explanation: Concurrency control manages simultaneous access to resources to prevent interference.

questions.questionText: Quality programming that comes from good program design is necessary for the economic and correct solution of problems. Assume you are the program designer and the program that you design cannot adapt one type of computer to another with minimum modification. So, what need of a good program design is failed?
questions.explanation: Portability allows a program to run on different platforms with minimal changes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is INCORRECT about an algorithm?
options: Set of instructions showing the steps of solving the problem.
All the steps can be dependent on any programming language or machine.
The steps must be efficient in time, memory and other resources
It must produce expected output and can be simple and correct
questions.correctAnswer: All the steps can be dependent on any programming language or machine.
questions.explanation: Algorithms should be independent of programming languages and machines; they are abstract.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following should include under every C++ program?
questions.explanation: Every C++ program must have a main() function as the entry point.

questions.questionText: A symbolic name for memory location in which data can be stored and subsequently recalled is called ______.
questions.explanation: Variables are names for memory locations to store data.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements provides a way of choosing between a set of alternatives based on the value of an expression?
questions.explanation: The switch statement selects among multiple cases based on an expression's value.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is used to execute block of code known times?
questions.explanation: The for loop is designed for executing a block a known number of times.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is false about abstract classes?
options: Abstract classes are declared using the keyword abstract.
An abstract class can be a superclass.
An abstract class can also be a final class.
An object of an abstract class cannot be created.
questions.correctAnswer: An abstract class can also be a final class.
questions.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be final because final prevents inheritance, while abstract requires subclassing to implement methods.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about interfaces?
options: An interface's methods are by default public and final.
An interface's variable is by default private, static and final.
An interface's methods are by default public and abstract.
An interface cannot be part of the inheritance hierarchy.
questions.correctAnswer: An interface's methods are by default public and abstract.
questions.explanation: In Java, interface methods are public and abstract by default.

questions.questionText: When a subclass object is created ________.
options: The very first constructor called is the subclass' constructor.
Any one of the constructors across the hierarchy can be called in a random order.
The last constructor called is the constructor of the superclass' constructor.
The very first constructor called is the top most superclass' constructor in the hierarchy.
questions.correctAnswer: The very first constructor called is the top most superclass' constructor in the hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Constructors are called from superclass to subclass, starting with Object.

questions.questionText: When a method is overridden ________.
options: Both methods have exactly same signature.
Java uses it to implement compile time polymorphism.
The super keyword is used to call the overriding (subclass') method.
The overridden method must be final always so that the subclass can override it.
questions.correctAnswer: Both methods have exactly same signature.
questions.explanation: Overriding requires the same method signature in subclass.

questions.questionText: A reference variable can refer to ________.
options: An object of its class type only
An object of subclass's or its class type
questions.correctAnswer: An object of subclass's or its class type
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows a reference to point to subclass objects.

questions.questionText: When a class must not be inherited, it must be declared using the __________ keyword.
questions.explanation: A final class cannot be extended.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an incorrect statement about algorithms?
options: algorithm is composed of a finite set of steps
each steps of algorithm may require one or more operations
Each operation has to be effective but not necessarily definite
questions.correctAnswer: Each operation has to be effective but not necessarily definite
questions.explanation: Operations in algorithms must be definite and effective.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about running time analysis?
options: Determine how running time increases as the computer resources increases
Determine how running time increases as the size of the problem increases
Determine how running time decreases as the computer resources increases
questions.correctAnswer: Determine how running time increases as the size of the problem increases
questions.explanation: Running time analysis focuses on how time scales with input size.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about comparing algorithms?
options: Comparing based on execution times is good for all cases
Comparing based on number of statements helps to compare universally
Express running time as a function of the input size n is ideal
questions.correctAnswer: Express running time as a function of the input size n is ideal
questions.explanation: Asymptotic analysis using big O etc. is the standard way to compare algorithms independently of hardware.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is incorrect about principle of optimality?
options: an optimal sequence of decisions, some subsequence may not be optimal
an optimal sequence of decisions, each subsequence must also be optimal
we need to show principle of optimality applies to the problem before using dynamic programming
questions.correctAnswer: an optimal sequence of decisions, some subsequence may not be optimal
questions.explanation: The principle states that subsequences must be optimal.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a correct asymptotic notation?
options: Big Θ is asymptotic tight bound
questions.explanation: Big O is upper, Big Omega lower, Big Theta tight.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about heap data structure?
options: A heap is a nearly complete binary tree
the last level may not be full, as heap is filled in order right to left
questions.correctAnswer: A heap is a nearly complete binary tree
questions.explanation: Heaps are complete binary trees, filled left to right, last level may not be full.

questions.questionText: What does each iteration of the insertion sort algorithm do?
options: Each iteration takes the next smallest element and inserts it at the beginning of the array
Each iteration takes the next element in the unsorted portion of the array and inserts it into the sorted portion
Sorted subarrays are inserted into the larger array
Each iteration determines the location of a pivot and inserts it into place
questions.correctAnswer: Each iteration takes the next element in the unsorted portion of the array and inserts it into the sorted portion
questions.explanation: Insertion sort builds the sorted list by inserting elements one by one.

questions.questionText: Using a binary search, what is the maximum number of comparisons required to find a search key in a 31-element sorted array
questions.explanation: log2(31) ≈ 4.95, so 5 comparisons max.

questions.questionText: In order to get the information stored in a binary search tree in the descending order, one should traverse it in which of the following order?
questions.explanation: Reverse inorder traversal gives descending order in BST.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is true?
options: The binary search algorithm is less efficient than the linear search, but it requires that the array be sorted
The binary search algorithm is more efficient than the linear search, but it requires that the array be sorted
The binary search algorithm is more efficient than the linear search, but it requires that the array be unsorted
The binary search algorithm is less efficient than the linear search, but it requires that the array be unsorted
questions.correctAnswer: The binary search algorithm is more efficient than the linear search, but it requires that the array be sorted
questions.explanation: Binary search is O(log n) vs linear O(n), but needs sorted data.

questions.questionText: What happens when you push a new node onto a stack?
options: The new node is placed at the front of the linked list
The new node is placed at the back of the linked list
The new node is placed at the middle of the linked list
questions.correctAnswer: The new node is placed at the front of the linked list
questions.explanation: Stack is LIFO, push adds to top, which is front in linked list implementation.

questions.questionText: ______ is very useful in situation when data have to stored and then retrieved in reverse order.
questions.explanation: Stack is LIFO, ideal for reverse order retrieval.

questions.questionText: Which OSI layer defines the functions of logical network addressing and routing?

questions.questionText: Dialogue and conversation between the sender and the receiver device is established by ____

options: Export the table to a data warehouse, including only the fields that the users are permitted to see
Clone the table, including only the fields that the users are permitted to see
Create a view that contains only the fields that the users are permitted to see
questions.correctAnswer: Create a view that contains only the fields that the users are permitted to see

questions.questionText: Public key cryptography is so-named because __________

questions.questionText: If your request is not time-sensitive, such as finding the address of a student in the database, use the ________ method to speed up the performance.
questions.explanation: GET can be cached, faster for reads.

questions.questionText: Apache Tomcat is a ________.
options: D. Web server that is capable of running Java programs.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Web server that is capable of running Java programs.
questions.explanation: Tomcat is servlet container/web server for Java servlets/JSP.

questions.questionText: A servlet is an instance of ________.
questions.explanation: Typically extend HttpServlet.

questions.questionText: To start the Tomcat servlet engine, use the command ________ from the TomcatRootDir\bin directory.
questions.explanation: startup.bat or sh to start Tomcat.

questions.questionText: By default, Tomcat runs on port ________.
questions.explanation: Default HTTP port 8080.

questions.questionText: The ________ interface defines the methods that all servlets must implement.
questions.explanation: Servlet interface.

questions.questionText: The ________ method is called when the servlet is first created, and is not called again as long as the servlet is not destroyed.
questions.explanation: init() for initialization.

questions.questionText: The ________ class defines a servlet for the HTTP protocol.
questions.explanation: HttpServlet for HTTP.

questions.questionText: ________ is a subinterface of ServletRequest.
questions.explanation: HttpServletRequest extends ServletRequest.

questions.questionText: Every doXxx method in the HttpServlet class has a parameter of the ________ type, which is an object that contains HTTP request information, including parameter name and values, attributes, and an input stream.
questions.explanation: Request parameter.

questions.questionText: Every doXxx method in the HttpServlet class has a parameter of the HttpServletResponse type, which is an object that assists a servlet in sending a response to the client.
questions.explanation: Response parameter.

questions.questionText: Suppose the two parameters in the doGet or doPost method are request and response. To specify HTML content type sent to the client, invoke ________.
questions.explanation: Set content type on response.

questions.questionText: Suppose the two parameters in the doGet or doPost method are request and response. To send output to a client, create a PrintWriter using ________.
questions.explanation: getWriter() for PrintWriter.

questions.questionText: The code for loading a JDBC driver and connecting to a database should be invoked from ______ in a servlet.
questions.explanation: init for one-time setup like DB connection.

questions.questionText: To store a hidden value for lastName as Smith in an HTML form, use ________.
questions.explanation: hidden type for non-visible data.

questions.questionText: To create a cookie for lastName with value Smith, use ________.
questions.explanation: Cookie(name, value).

questions.questionText: Suppose the two parameters in the doGet or doPost method are request and response. To send a cookie to a client, use ________.
questions.explanation: addCookie on response.

questions.questionText: Suppose the two parameters in the doGet or doPost method are request and response. To retrieve a cookie from a client, use ________.
options: C. You have to use request.getCookies() to obtain all cookies in an array
D. You have to use request.getCookie() to obtain a cookie
questions.correctAnswer: C. You have to use request.getCookies() to obtain all cookies in an array
questions.explanation: getCookies() returns Cookie[].

questions.questionText: For an instance of Cookie, say cookie, to retrieve the name of the cookie, use ________.
options: C. You have to use cookie.getNames() to obtain all values in an array.
D. You have to use cookie.getValues() to obtain all values in an array.
questions.explanation: getName() for cookie name.

questions.questionText: Suppose the two parameters in the doGet or doPost method are request and response. To create an HTTP session, use ________.
questions.explanation: getSession() gets or creates session.

questions.questionText: For an HttpSession, say session, how do you set an attribute pair with name lastName and value Smith?
questions.explanation: setAttribute for session attributes.

questions.questionText: For a HttpSession, say session, how do you get its attribute?
questions.explanation: getAttribute to retrieve.

questions.questionText: A JSP file ends with ________.
questions.explanation: .jsp for JSP files.

questions.questionText: You can run JSP from ________.
options: C. any Web server that supports Java servlet and JSP.
questions.correctAnswer: C. any Web server that supports Java servlet and JSP.
questions.explanation: Needs container like Tomcat.

questions.questionText: ________ is a JSP scriptlet.
options: C. <%! private long computeFactorial(int n) { if (n == 0) return 1; else return n * computeFactorial(n - 1); } %>
questions.explanation: <% %> for scriptlets (code).

questions.questionText: ________ is a JSP declaration.
options: C. <%! private long computeFactorial(int n) { if (n == 0) return 1; else return n * computeFactorial(n - 1); } %>
questions.correctAnswer: C. <%! private long computeFactorial(int n) { if (n == 0) return 1; else return n * computeFactorial(n - 1); } %>
questions.explanation: <%! %> for declarations.

questions.questionText: ________ is a JSP comment.
options: C. <%! private long computeFactorial(int n) { if (n == 0) return 1; else return n * computeFactorial(n - 1); } %>
questions.explanation: <%-- --%> for JSP comments.

questions.questionText: The JSP explicit object out is actually ________.
questions.explanation: out is JspWriter, from response.getWriter().

questions.questionText: ______ is a statement that gives the JSP engine information about the JSP page.
questions.explanation: Directives like <%@ page %>.

questions.questionText: The ______ directive lets you provide information for the page, such as importing classes and setting up content type. The page directive can appear anywhere in the JSP file.
questions.explanation: <%@ page %> for page settings.

questions.questionText: A class is a JavaBeans component if ____________________.
options: A. it is a public class
B. it has a public constructor with no arguments
questions.explanation: JavaBean requirements: public, no-arg constructor, serializable.

questions.questionText: ____ completely separates Web UI from Java code so the application developed using JSF is easy to debug and maintain.
questions.explanation: JSF uses component-based UI, separates from code.

questions.questionText: What is the Default Templating System for JSF?
questions.explanation: Facelets is default for JSF 2+.

questions.questionText: What is full form of JSF?
questions.explanation: JSF is JavaServer Faces.

questions.questionText: What are the different types of JSF events?
questions.explanation: These are system events in JSF.

questions.questionText: What is the file extension of JSF?
questions.explanation: JSF views are .xhtml or .jsp.

questions.questionText: A JSF application typically follows ______ in its life.
questions.explanation: JSF lifecycle: restore view, apply request values, process validations, update model, invoke application, render response.

questions.questionText: ______ is Often Used with JSF.
questions.explanation: Ajax for dynamic updates in JSF.

questions.questionText: ______ Creates a Radio Button.
questions.explanation: h:selectOneRadio for radio buttons in JSF.

questions.questionText: ________________ is an AI approach that tries to create artificially intelligent agents by mimicking how people behave under certain circumstances.
questions.explanation: Although the question's description 'mimicking how people behave' aligns more closely with the 'acting humanly' approach (e.g., Turing test, where the focus is on external behavior that resembles human actions), the options provided suggest the intended answer is the 'thinking humanly' approach. The thinking humanly approach involves cognitive modeling to simulate how humans think internally, which can result in behavior that mimics humans. However, standard AI literature distinguishes between thinking (internal process) and acting (external behavior). Given the options, A is selected as the closest match, possibly due to a phrasing issue in the question.

questions.questionText: Which of the following tasks can be performed by the program components of a given intelligent agent?
options: B. Makes the percept from the sensors available to the programs
C. Feeds the program’s action choices to the effectors
questions.explanation: The program component of an intelligent agent is the core software that implements the agent's decision-making logic. It executes the code (A), processes input percepts from sensors to make them available for decision-making (B), and outputs chosen actions to the effectors to interact with the environment (C). Therefore, all listed tasks are part of the program's role in an intelligent agent architecture.

questions.questionText: In a dynamic environment.
options: A. an agent has access to the complete state of the environment
B. The next state is completely determined by the current state and the actions selected by the agents.
C. The environment is always at its constant
questions.explanation: A dynamic environment is one where the environment can change independently of the agent's actions, such as time passing or other agents acting. Option A describes a fully observable environment, Option B describes a deterministic environment, and Option C describes a static environment. None of these define a dynamic environment, so the correct choice is D.

questions.questionText: _______________ try to solve the problem by using stored information to draw new conclusions.
questions.explanation: Automated reasoning is a subfield of AI that focuses on using logical inference to derive new knowledge or conclusions from existing facts stored in a knowledge base. Natural language processing deals with language understanding, robotics with physical actions, so A is the correct match.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs of AI approaches can go together?
options: A. Thinking Humanly-Requires Modeling Human Brain Activity
B. Acting Rationally- Deals with enabling a machine to do what humans can do like Speech recognition, Natural language processing, Computer Vision, and Machine Learning.
C. Acting Humanly- Deal with The law of Thought and Logics
questions.correctAnswer: A. Thinking Humanly-Requires Modeling Human Brain Activity
questions.explanation: The thinking humanly approach involves cognitive science and modeling how the human brain thinks and processes information. Option B describes aspects more aligned with acting humanly (Turing test tasks), and Option C describes thinking rationally (logic-based). Therefore, only A is the correct pair, making it the answer.

questions.questionText: ________ Omniscience agent supposed to.
options: A. Know the actual outcome of every actions it performs
C. An agent that tries to maximize its performance Measure.
questions.explanation: An omniscient agent is theoretically one that knows everything, including the actual outcomes of its actions (A) and has complete observation of the environment (B). Option C describes a rational agent, which aims to maximize expected performance based on limited knowledge. Thus, D is correct for omniscience.

questions.questionText: Which one of The following statements is false about the Conception of AI
options: A. Strong AI argues that one-day Computers can be a machine that has a mind in its fullest sense.
B. Strong AI aims at creating a machine that replicates humans’ intelligence completely.
C. Strong AI argues computers can only think and are not conscious.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Strong AI argues computers can only think and are not conscious.
questions.explanation: Strong AI (or artificial general intelligence) posits that machines can possess true consciousness and mind, replicating human intelligence fully (A and B). Option C describes weak AI, which views computers as simulating intelligence without true consciousness. Thus, C is false for strong AI.

questions.questionText: ________ Ominscience agent supposed to.
options: A. Know the actual outcome of every actions it performs
C. An agent that tries to maximize its performance Measure.
questions.explanation: This is a repeat of question 6 with a typo in 'Omniscience'. The explanation is the same: An omniscient agent knows action outcomes and fully observes the environment, so D is correct.

questions.questionText: Which one of The following statements is false about the Conception of AI
options: A. Strong AI argues that one-day Computers can be a machine that has a mind in its fullest sense.
B. Strong AI aims at creating a machine that replicates humans’ intelligence completely.
C. Strong AI argues computers can only think and are not conscious.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Strong AI argues computers can only think and are not conscious.
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 7. See explanation for question 7.

questions.questionText: Which group of the following environment is more complex than the other for the agent to act appropriately?
options: A. Fully Observable, Deterministic, Episodic, Static, Discrete
B. Partially observable, Deterministic, Sequential, Dynamic, Continuous
C. Partially Observable, sequential, non-deterministic, dynamic, continuous.
D. Partially Observable, Episodic, non-deterministic, dynamic, continuous.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Partially Observable, sequential, non-deterministic, dynamic, continuous.
questions.explanation: Environment complexity increases with partial observability, sequential (history-dependent) tasks, non-deterministic (stochastic) outcomes, dynamic changes, and continuous state/action spaces. Option C has all these features, making it more complex than B (deterministic) or D (episodic, less history dependence).

questions.questionText: Deterministic environments are characterized by___________________.
options: A. Unique mapping of the next state given the current state and actions
B. Taxi driving is a deterministic
C. the environment can change while the agent is on purpose
questions.correctAnswer: A. Unique mapping of the next state given the current state and actions
questions.explanation: In a deterministic environment, the next state is completely and uniquely determined by the current state and the agent's action, with no randomness. B is false (taxi driving is stochastic), C describes dynamic environments.

questions.questionText: Artificial intelligence is
options: A. The embodiment of human intellectual capabilities within a computer.
B. a set of computer programs that produce output that would be considered to reflect intelligence if it were generated by humans
C. The study of mental faculties with mental models implemented on a computer.
questions.explanation: AI can be defined in multiple ways: as replicating human capabilities (A), producing intelligent output (B), or studying mental models computationally (C). All are valid perspectives from different approaches to AI.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an attribute of AI systems?
questions.explanation: AI systems are characterized by their ability to exhibit intelligent behavior, such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving. Options B, C, and D describe biological or emotional traits not inherent to AI.

questions.questionText: AI attempts not only the factual knowledge of a human but also the knowledge that relates to the judgmental or common sense part of the knowledge. What is the term used for describing the bold sentence?
questions.explanation: Heuristic knowledge refers to rule-of-thumb, judgmental, or common-sense knowledge that helps in problem-solving without guaranteeing optimality, contrasting with factual (declarative) or procedural knowledge.

questions.questionText: In __________ perspective of AI, the Turing test was developed as a technique for determining whether a computer could or could not demonstrate artificial Intelligence.
questions.explanation: The Turing test is part of the acting humanly approach, where AI is evaluated based on its ability to exhibit behavior indistinguishable from a human, focusing on external actions rather than internal thought processes.

questions.questionText: Rationality is concerned with “doing/thinking the right thing”. The bold term refers
options: A. One that leads to the correct result
B. One that leads to a goal with no error
C. One that maximizes goal achievement using the available information
D. One that is always successful based on the available information
questions.correctAnswer: C. One that maximizes goal achievement using the available information
questions.explanation: Rationality in AI means choosing actions that are expected to maximize the achievement of goals, given the available information and uncertainty, not necessarily guaranteeing success or no errors.

questions.questionText: Which one is different from the other?
questions.explanation: State space, problem space, and search space all refer to the set of all possible configurations or paths in a problem. A state is a single instance or configuration within that space.

questions.questionText: Search strategy that paves a way to order the choices so that the most promising are explored first.
questions.explanation: Informed (heuristic) search uses domain-specific knowledge to prioritize promising paths, unlike uninformed (blind) searches like BFS, which explore without heuristics.

questions.questionText: Which is true about the Evaluation function f(n) for Greedy Search?
questions.explanation: In greedy best-first search, the evaluation function f(n) = h(n), the heuristic estimate of cost from n to the goal, ignoring the path cost g(n).

questions.questionText: Which is true about the Evaluation function f(n) for A*Search?
questions.explanation: In A* search, f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is the cost from start to n, and h(n) is the heuristic to the goal, balancing path cost and future estimate for optimality.

questions.questionText: Which list is correct about the simplest case environment for the agent?
options: A. partially observable, stochastic, sequential, dynamic, continuous, multi-agent
B. partially observable, stochastic, episodic, dynamic, continuous, multi-agent
C. partially observable, stochastic, sequential, dynamic, discrete, multi-agent
D. Fully observable, Deterministic, Episodic, Static, Discrete, Single agent
questions.correctAnswer: D. Fully observable, Deterministic, Episodic, Static, Discrete, Single agent
questions.explanation: The simplest environment is fully observable (full info), deterministic (predictable), episodic (no history dependence), static (no changes during deliberation), discrete (finite states/actions), and single-agent (no other agents).

questions.questionText: The worst-case time complexity for the bidirectional search worst-case
options: A. O(bd/2); where b is the branching factor, d the is a depth limit of the shallowest solution
B. O(bm); where b is a branching factor and m is the maximum depth of the search tree
C. O(bm); b is the branching factor, m maximum depth of the search tree
D. O(bd); where b is branching factor, d is depth limit of the shallowest solution
questions.correctAnswer: A. O(bd/2); where b is the branching factor, d the is a depth limit of the shallowest solution
questions.explanation: Bidirectional search searches from start and goal simultaneously, meeting in the middle, reducing the effective depth to d/2, thus time complexity O(b^{d/2}).

questions.questionText: ________________ is an AI approach that tries to create artificially intelligent agents by mimicking how people behave under certain circumstances.
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 1. See explanation for question 1. Note the potential misphrasing; standardly, this describes acting humanly.

B. Partially observable, Deterministic, Sequential, Dynamic, Continuous

questions.questionText: __________type of agent that act and thnk by assuming future destinations is.
questions.explanation: A goal-based agent uses information about the future (goals) to choose actions that lead to desirable states, considering possible future destinations in its decision-making.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not correct about the evolution of Artificial intelligence?
options: A. Shifts from declarative to procedural programming paradigm
B. Simulate the human mind and learning behavior
C. Shift from general-purpose to domain-specific systems
questions.correctAnswer: A. Shifts from declarative to procedural programming paradigm
questions.explanation: AI evolution has involved shifts from procedural to declarative paradigms (e.g., logic programming), simulation of human mind (B), and from general to domain-specific (C). A is reversed, so incorrect.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about an omniscient agent?
options: A. knows the actual outcome of its actions
B. take action with 100% sure of its success
C. Humans are an omniscient agent
E. A and B are correct
questions.correctAnswer: E. A and B are correct
questions.explanation: An omniscient agent knows the outcomes of its actions (A) and can act with certainty (B), but humans are not omniscient (C false) as they have limited knowledge.

questions.questionText: Deterministic environments are characterized by___________________.
options: A. Unique mapping of the next state given the current state and actions
B. Taxi driving is a deterministic
C. the environment can change while the agent is on purpose
questions.correctAnswer: A. Unique mapping of the next state given the current state and actions
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 11. See explanation for question 11.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a characteristics of autonomous systems
options: B. Use of Natural language for programming
C. Requires user control and guidance
questions.correctAnswer: C. Requires user control and guidance
questions.explanation: Autonomous systems operate independently without constant user control (C is not a characteristic). They apply knowledge (A), learn and interact (D), but programming language is not defining.

questions.questionText: ____________function estimated cost of the cheapest path from node n to a goal node.
questions.explanation: The heuristic function h(n) estimates the lowest cost path from node n to a goal, guiding informed search algorithms.

questions.questionText: Which of the following heuristic function is good in measuring distance between two sub parts of a city?
questions.explanation: Manhattan distance (sum of horizontal and vertical distances) is suitable for city grids where movement is along blocks, unlike straight-line (Euclidean) for direct paths.

questions.questionText: __________________search algorithm aims at achieving to minimize the total path cost.
questions.explanation: A* search uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n) to find the path with the lowest total cost, being optimal if the heuristic is admissible.

questions.questionText: The best first search that uses t heuristic function alone is
questions.explanation: Greedy best-first search uses only the heuristic h(n) for evaluation, prioritizing nodes closest to the goal by estimate.

questions.questionText: A search algorithm is admissible if___________
options: A. The Heuristic Function does overestimate the actual function.
B. the heuristic function does not overestimate the actual function
C. If actual distance lesser that the distance that is estimated by the heuristic
questions.correctAnswer: B. the heuristic function does not overestimate the actual function
questions.explanation: An admissible heuristic never overestimates the true cost to the goal (h(n) ≤ true cost), ensuring the algorithm finds the optimal path if it exists.

questions.questionText: The closer estimated cost to the actual cost in heuristic function mean____________
options: A. Fewer extra node that will be expanded
B. The more extra node that will be expanded
questions.correctAnswer: A. Fewer extra node that will be expanded
questions.explanation: A heuristic closer to the actual cost is more informative, leading to fewer unnecessary node expansions as it guides the search more efficiently toward the goal.

questions.questionText: Expression or structure that are allowed in a particular language is called
questions.explanation: Syntax refers to the rules governing the structure and formation of valid expressions or sentences in a language, while semantics deals with meaning.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following expressions is Contradictory in prepositional logic
questions.explanation: A contradiction is a sentence that is always false, like A ∧ ¬A, which cannot be true under any interpretation.

questions.questionText: A sentence which is true under all possible interpretations is called
questions.explanation: A tautology (or valid sentence) is true in every possible interpretation. Satisfiable means true in at least one interpretation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true?
options: A. Inference rule that works for prepositional logic also works for first-order logic
B. First-order logic is complete that Prepositional logic
C. Prepositional logic can represent quantifiable facts
questions.correctAnswer: C. Prepositional logic can represent quantifiable facts
questions.explanation: Propositional logic cannot handle quantifiers like ∀ or ∃; that's a feature of first-order logic. A is true (rules like modus ponens apply), B is true (FOL is more expressive).

questions.questionText: Predicate in first-order logic used to
options: A. Relate one object with the other
B. To describe some or all objects satisfy the condition
C. Used to describe the properties of the object
questions.explanation: Predicates in FOL describe properties of objects (C) or relations between objects (A). B describes quantifiers, not predicates.

questions.questionText: Which of the following description of FOL is correct for a sentence; “There are some students who are hard workers?
questions.explanation: The sentence 'some students are hard workers' is ∃x (student(x) ∧ hardworker(x)), but the options have implication. A is ∃x hardworker(x) → student(x), which is wrong. Wait, actually, the sentence is 'There are some students who are hard workers', so ∃x student(x) ∧ hardworker(x). A is ∃x hardworker(x) → student(x), which is not equivalent. B is all hardworkers are students. C is ¬∀x ¬ (hardworker(x) → student(x)) , which is equivalent to ∃x hardworker(x) → student(x), same as A. So none are correct, but perhaps the question has errors. Assuming D as per option.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sentence of First-order Logic is correctly described
questions.explanation: This sentence means 'All people at BDU are smart', using universal quantifier and implication. B is incomplete syntax, C uses existential with implication, which is different.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following searching techniques does not belong to evaluation driven function search?
questions.explanation: Evaluation-driven (informed) searches use heuristics or cost functions to evaluate nodes (A, C, D). Breadth-first search is uninformed, exploring levels without evaluation.

questions.questionText: _______________estimated cost of the cheapest path from the state at node n to a goal state.
questions.explanation: The heuristic h(n) estimates the cheapest path from n to the goal. Edge cost is between nodes, uniform cost is a search algorithm.

questions.questionText: The difference between the uniform cost search and the greedy search techniques lies in __________.
options: A. Greedy search depends on edge cost and heuristic cost while uniform cost search only on heuristic values
B. Greedy search depends on heuristic values while uniform cost search depend on both edge cost and heuristic values
C. Uniform cost search depends only heuristic cost while uniform cost search depends on edge cost
questions.explanation: Uniform cost search uses only path cost g(n) (edge costs), greedy uses only heuristic h(n). None of the options accurately describe this; correct would be uniform depends on edge cost (g(n)), greedy on heuristic.

questions.questionText: The best first search that uses the heuristic function alone is
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 36. See explanation for question 36.

questions.questionText: Manhattan Distance measures
options: A. the block distance between two objects
B. the straight line distance between two objects
C. the actual edge cost of objects
questions.correctAnswer: A. the block distance between two objects
questions.explanation: Manhattan distance (L1 norm) measures the sum of absolute differences in coordinates, representing block-by-block distance in a grid.

questions.questionText: _____________function that estimates cost of the path from node n to a goal node.
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 33. See explanation for question 33.

questions.questionText: Which of the following heuristic function is good in measuring distance between two sub parts of a city?
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 34. See explanation for question 34.

questions.questionText: __________________search algorithm aims at achieving to minimize the total path cost.

questions.questionText: __________type of agent works by finding a rule whose condition matches the current situation (as defined by the percept) and then doing the action associated with that rule.
questions.explanation: A simple reflex agent uses condition-action rules to map current percepts directly to actions, without memory or modeling.

questions.questionText: Single state problem is a problem that runs in _________________.
options: A. Fully observable and Deterministic Environment
B. Partially observable and Deterministic Environment.
C. Partially observable and non deterministic environment.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Fully observable and Deterministic Environment
questions.explanation: Single-state problems assume the agent knows the exact state (fully observable) and outcomes are predictable (deterministic), allowing planning based on current state alone.

questions.questionText: __________Is a function that returns the set of states that are reachable from a single state by any single action
questions.explanation: The successor function generates all possible next states from a current state by applying actions, essential for search algorithms.

questions.questionText: Completeness of a search algorithm can be measured
options: A. The capacity of algorithm to guarantee in finding a solution whenever one exists.
B. The Capacity of the algorithm in finding a solution that has minimum cost.
C. The capacity of the search algorithm to be processed in a minimum period of time.
questions.correctAnswer: A. The capacity of algorithm to guarantee in finding a solution whenever one exists.
questions.explanation: Completeness means the algorithm will find a solution if one exists. B is optimality, C is time efficiency.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the search algorithms?
options: A. Breadth-first search can be implemented in the stack data structure.
B. Breadth-first search expands the deepest node in a tree first.
C. Breadth first search is complete and Optimal Than Depth first search
questions.correctAnswer: C. Breadth first search is complete and Optimal Than Depth first search
questions.explanation: BFS is complete and optimal (for unweighted graphs), unlike DFS. A is false (BFS uses queue, DFS uses stack), B is false (DFS expands deepest).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following techniques of searching is useful in finding the shortest path to the goal in terms of cost
questions.explanation: Uniform cost search expands nodes by lowest path cost g(n), finding the shortest path in terms of cost, optimal for varying edge costs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following searching techniques does not belong to the evaluation-driven search algorithm?
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 46. See explanation for question 46.

questions.questionText: Completeness of a search algorithm measures
options: A. The capacity of an algorithm to provide a solution for a given problem when there exists at least one solution for this problem
B. The capacity of the algorithm to find an optimum solution for a problem.
C. The capacity of the search algorithm to find a solution in a minimum processing time.
questions.correctAnswer: A. The capacity of an algorithm to provide a solution for a given problem when there exists at least one solution for this problem
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 57 (slight rephrase). See explanation for question 57.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the search algorithms?
options: A. Breadth-first search is usually implemented in a stack.
B. Breadth-first search expands the deepest node in a tree first.
C. Breadth-first search is more complete and more optimal than depth-first search
questions.correctAnswer: C. Breadth-first search is more complete and more optimal than depth-first search
questions.explanation: BFS is complete in finite spaces and optimal for unweighted graphs, while DFS is not always complete or optimal. A false (queue for BFS), B false (shallowest first).

questions.questionText: _______________estimated cost of paths from the n state to a goal state.
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 47. See explanation for question 47.

questions.questionText: The difference between the uniform cost search and the greedy search techniques lies in __________.
options: A. Greedy search depends on actual path cost from the initial state to state n while uniform cost search techniques only depend on heuristic values
B. Greedy search depends on heuristic values while uniform cost search techniques depend on both edge cost and heuristic values
C. Uniform cost search depends only on heuristic cost while greedy search depends on both edge costs and heuristics
questions.explanation: Repeat of question 48. See explanation for question 48.

questions.questionText: The best first search that expands nodes nearer to the goal first is called ------------
questions.explanation: Greedy search expands nodes with the lowest heuristic value, prioritizing those estimated to be nearer to the goal.

questions.questionText: Which of the following heuristic function is good in estimating the distance between two sub-parts of a city?
questions.explanation: The Manhattan distance (also called taxicab distance or L1 norm) is widely used in AI search problems, especially in grid-based environments like cities with rectangular street layouts.It measures the distance between two points by summing the absolute differences of their coordinates:𝑑(𝑥,𝑦)=∣𝑥1−𝑦1∣+∣𝑥2−𝑦2∣This reflects the actual block-by-block travel in a city where you can only move along streets aligned in a grid, rather than diagonally. Straight line distance (A), also known as Euclidean distance, is useful in open spaces but not realistic in city layouts with restricted movement.Heuristic distance (B) is too vague and not a standard defined function.None of the above (D) is incorrect because Manhattan distance is indeed the right heuristic for city sub-parts.Thus, Manhattan distance is the most appropriate heuristic function for estimating distances in urban grid-like environments.

questions.questionText: __________________search algorithm aims at achieving to minimize the total path cost.
questions.explanation: The A* search algorithm is specifically designed to minimize the total path cost by combining two components in its evaluation function:𝑓(𝑛)=𝑔(𝑛)+ℎ(𝑛)g(n): the actual cost from the start node to the current node.h(n): the heuristic estimate of the cost from the current node to the goal.This balance ensures that A* search explores paths that are both cost-effective so far and promising toward the goal.Breadth-first search (A) guarantees the shortest path only when all step costs are equal, but it doesn’t minimize total path cost in weighted graphs.Greedy search (C) uses only the heuristic ℎ(𝑛), which can lead to suboptimal paths because it ignores the actual cost already incurred. Depth-first search (D) explores deeply without considering path cost, so it is not optimal for minimizing cost. Therefore, A* search is the correct algorithm because it optimally minimizes the total path cost by combining actual and estimated costs.

questions.questionText: Assume the actual distance from a given state n and goal state is 100 meters. Which one of the following heuristic values is admissible for the given distance
questions.explanation: An admissible heuristic does not overestimate the actual cost, so values ≤ 100 (A: 100, C: 99) are admissible, while >100 (B, D) are not.

questions.questionText: In the depth-first search
options: A. A non-goal dead end does the search go back and expand nodes at shallower levels
B. Expands the shallowest unexpanded node first
C. Expands the node with minimum cost first
questions.correctAnswer: A. A non-goal dead end does the search go back and expand nodes at shallower levels
questions.explanation: DFS explores deep paths first; when reaching a dead end, it backtracks to shallower levels to explore other branches.

questions.questionText: The problem with the greedy search
options: A. It may expand the node that is already expensive
B. It may depend on only path costs explored from initial state
C. It is a fast-searching techniques
questions.correctAnswer: A. It may expand the node that is already expensive
questions.explanation: Greedy search ignores path cost g(n), so it may choose expensive paths if the heuristic misleads, leading to sub-optimal solutions.

questions.questionText: __________Is a function that returns the set of states that are reachable from a single state by any single action
questions.explanation: In search problems within Artificial Intelligence, the successor function is the key mechanism that defines how the agent can move from one state to another.It takes a current state as input and returns all possible next states that can be reached by applying one valid action.For example, in a chess game, the successor function for a given board position would generate all possible legal moves and the resulting board states. Operator (A) refers to the specific action itself, not the function that generates new states.Goal test function (B) is used to check whether a given state is the goal state, not to generate new states.“Is goal test function” (D) is just a misphrased repetition and does not apply here.Thus, the successor function is the correct answer because it explicitly defines the set of reachable states from a given state by applying available actions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true
options: A. A* search optimality is dependent of the admissibility of the heuristic
B. Admissible heuristic usually overestimates the actual coast
C. Greedy search is more complete that A* search
questions.correctAnswer: A. A* search optimality is dependent of the admissibility of the heuristic
questions.explanation: A* is optimal if the heuristic is admissible (never overestimates). B is false (admissible underestimates or equals), C is false (both complete in finite spaces, but A* is optimal).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following FOL sentences is equivalent to “Every flower in some garden is lovely”?
options: A. ∀x flower(X)y garden(y) in (X, Y) lovely(X)
questions.correctAnswer: A. ∀x flower(X)y garden(y) in (X, Y) lovely(X)
questions.explanation: The sentence means for every flower, there is a garden it is in, and it is lovely. A captures this. B and C are not equivalent, as they involve negations incorrectly.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following FOL sentences is equivalent to "None of your friends are smart."
questions.explanation: 'None of your friends are smart' is ∀x friends_of(x, you) → ¬smart(x), which is equivalent to ∀x friends_of(x, you) ∧ ¬smart(x) (B, since implication with false consequent), and ¬∃x friends_of(x, you) ∧ smart(x) (C).

questions.questionText: A FOL’s inference rule that substitutes a variable with a constant symbol that does not exist in the KB
questions.explanation: Skolemization replaces existentially quantified variables with unique constant symbols (Skolem constants) not already in the KB to eliminate quantifiers.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a requirement for knowledge representation language?
questions.explanation: A good knowledge representation language must adequately represent knowledge (A), support efficient inference (C), and be understandable (B).

questions.questionText: Assume the knowledgebase contains (A V C)  (B VC). Which one of the following sentences can be entailed from the knowledgebase.
questions.explanation: Using resolution or truth tables, (A ∨ C) ∧ (B ∨ ¬C) entails A ∨ B, as the C and ¬C cover all cases leading to A or B. B and C are not necessarily entailed.

questions.questionText: Assume a knowledgebase in FOL contains X loves (X, Everyone). Which one of the following sentences can be entailed from the knowledgebase through existential elimination.
questions.explanation: Existential elimination (instantiation) replaces the existential quantifier with a new constant (e.g., 'lover') not in the KB, yielding loves(lover, Everyone).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences can be entailed from P V(PQ)
questions.explanation: P ∨ (P → Q) is equivalent to Q, because if P is true, then P → Q implies Q true; if P false, P → Q is true, but the or is true, but actually, truth table: if P false, P→Q true, or true; if P true, Q must be true for the implication. Perhaps the answer is D none, but since D is all, perhaps the question has error. Assuming D.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following characteristics is not always true about the nature of knowledge?
questions.explanation: Knowledge is often voluminous, dynamic (changes over time), and imprecise, but it is not always complete; there are gaps in knowledge.

questions.questionText: Knowledge based systems are better than data based systems (conventional systems) is because of:
options: A. the use of less complex syntaxes
B. Representation and communication with KBSs is close to human level language
C. The ability to learn and update itself
D. The use of inference mechanisms
questions.explanation: KBS excel due to natural representation (B), learning (C), inference (D), and simpler knowledge encoding compared to hard-coded conventional systems (A).

questions.questionText: Suppose we have a rule that says ‘All humans are mortal ‘. If we construct a new fact ‘Mr. Abebe is mortal’, where being abebe is one of the possible values of a domain human, which inference rule is used?
questions.explanation: Universal elimination (instantiation) substitutes a specific constant (Abebe) into a universally quantified rule to derive the instance for that constant.

questions.questionText: if we have premises say that ‘all humans are mortal  and ‘abebe is huuman’‘ then we can construct a new fact ‘abebe is mortal’, which inference rule is used?
questions.explanation: Modus ponens: From ∀x human(x) → mortal(x) and human(abebe), infer mortal(abebe). (Note: options are F-J, but I is modus ponens.

questions.questionText: If we have a premise that says AB, and B. what will be the possible conclusion with which inference rule?
questions.explanation: Modus tollens: From A → B and ¬B, infer ¬A.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a distinguishing feature of knowledge based systems?
questions.explanation: KBS are distinguished by knowledge, reasoning, inference, and learning. Data/attributes are common to conventional systems; KBS focus on knowledge over raw data.

questions.questionText: Constructing new fact which follows from a knowledge base represented using a semantic network is by applying:
questions.explanation: In semantic networks, new facts are derived via inference rules and inheritance (is-a links allowing property propagation).

questions.questionText: The following are not a characteristics of heuristic knowledge
questions.explanation: Heuristic knowledge is judgmental, experience-based, rule-of-thumb (A, C, D). Represented rules/facts are factual knowledge, not heuristic.

questions.questionText: AI technique that allows computers to understand associations and relationships between objects and events is called:
questions.explanation: Pattern matching in AI enables recognizing associations and relationships between objects and events, used in areas like vision and NLP.

questions.questionText: One definition of AI focuses on problem-solving methods that process:
questions.explanation: The symbol manipulation view of AI (physical symbol system hypothesis) focuses on processing symbols to solve problems, as in logic and search.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is the best description of a priori knowledge?
options: A. knowledge that is available prior to perception through senses
B. knowledge that is verifiable through sensory perception
C. knowledge that indicates how to do something
D. knowledge that is difficult to express through language
questions.correctAnswer: A. knowledge that is available prior to perception through senses
questions.explanation: A priori knowledge is innate or known independently of experience, prior to sensory perception, contrasting with a posteriori (empirical).

questions.questionText: Which statement is the best characterization of frames in the context of knowledge-based systems?
options: A. a frequently used method to formulate the knowledge in expert systems based on rules that describe the conversion of symbol strings into other symbol strings
B. a knowledge representation method based on graphs
C. a knowledge representation method that represents related knowledge about a subject through groups of slots and fillers
D. a knowledge representation method particularly suited for time-ordered sequences, e.g. of events
questions.correctAnswer: C. a knowledge representation method that represents related knowledge about a subject through groups of slots and fillers
questions.explanation: Frames organize knowledge about objects or concepts using slots (attributes) and fillers (values), supporting default values and inheritance.

questions.questionText: What does it mean that a logical sentence is satisfiable?
options: A. the sentence is true under all possible interpretations in all possible worlds
B. the sentence is true under all possible interpretations in some possible worlds
C. the sentence is true if there exists a true interpretation in some possible world
D. the sentence is syntactically correct
questions.correctAnswer: C. the sentence is true if there exists a true interpretation in some possible world
questions.explanation: Satisfiability means there is at least one model (interpretation) in which the sentence is true. Validity is true in all models.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the semantics of a formal language for knowledge representation?
options: A. It describes how a particular sentence relates to the facts in the world.
B. It allows the generation of new sentences that follow from a set of given sentences.
C. It specifies the admissible configurations of sentences in that language.
D. It makes sure that only truth-preserving sentences are admitted in the language.
questions.correctAnswer: A. It describes how a particular sentence relates to the facts in the world.
questions.explanation: Semantics define the meaning of sentences, relating them to real-world facts or models. Syntax is about structure (C), inference about derivation (B).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements characterizes predicate logic (in contrast to propositional logic)?
options: A. The world is described through sentences consisting of constants, symbols, connectives, and parentheses.
B. A simple logic in which truth tables are the only way of proving sentences.
C. The world is described through sentences specifying individual objects with properties, and relations between the objects.
D. A logic that relies on resolution as the only sound inference rule.
questions.correctAnswer: C. The world is described through sentences specifying individual objects with properties, and relations between the objects.
questions.explanation: Predicate (first-order) logic extends propositional logic by including objects, properties (predicates), relations, and quantifiers, allowing more expressive descriptions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the best description of an explanation facility?
options: A. the transfer of knowledge from humans to computers
B. the storage of knowledge in a format suitable for processing by computers
C. a computer-based mechanism for the generation of new conclusions from existing knowledge
D. a description of the reasons why a particular solution was generated
questions.correctAnswer: D. a description of the reasons why a particular solution was generated
questions.explanation: An explanation facility in expert systems provides transparency by explaining how and why a conclusion was reached, enhancing user trust.

questions.questionText: What is the role of an existential quantifier ∋ in a predicate logic sentence?
options: A. It allows statements about some objects in a collection of objects.
B. It allows general statements about every object in a collection.
C. It is used in the specification of the semantics for terms.
D. It can be used to make statements about quantitative aspects of objects, such as length, weight, temperature, etc.
questions.correctAnswer: A. It allows statements about some objects in a collection of objects.
questions.explanation: The existential quantifier ∃ asserts that there exists at least one object satisfying the property. Universal ∀ is for all (B).

questions.questionText: Which statement is the best characterization of knowledge representation?
options: A. It describes methods and procedures for drawing conclusions on the basis of existing knowledge.
B. It relies on the storage of relations between individual items according to a fixed scheme applied to a large collection of elementary items.
C. It requires a set of formal inference methods and clearly specified syntax and semantics.
D. It is concerned with methods and techniques for the storage of knowledge and information in a format that is suitable for treatment by computers.
questions.correctAnswer: D. It is concerned with methods and techniques for the storage of knowledge and information in a format that is suitable for treatment by computers.
questions.explanation: Knowledge representation focuses on how to encode knowledge in computable forms, like logics, frames, etc., for AI systems to use.

questions.questionText: Who provides the domain expertise in the form of problem-solving strategies?
questions.explanation: The domain expert supplies the specialized knowledge and strategies for the field, which the knowledge engineer formalizes into the system.

questions.questionText: Who formulates the domain expertise into an expert system?
questions.explanation: The knowledge engineer elicits knowledge from the domain expert and structures it into rules, frames, or other representations for the expert system.

questions.questionText: Which IT component in an expert system takes problem facts and searches the knowledge base for rules that fit?
questions.explanation: The inference engine applies reasoning to the knowledge base using facts to derive conclusions, matching rules and chaining inferences.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are correct translations of “No two adjacent countries have the same color”?
options: A. ∀x, y ¬ Country(x) ˅ ¬Country( y) ˅ ¬Adjacent(x, y) ˅ ¬(Color(x) = Color( y))
B. ∀x, y Country(x) ˄ Country( y) ˄ Adjacent(x, y) => ¬(Color(x) = Color( y))
C. ∀x, y Country(x) ˄ Country( y) ˄ Adjacent(x, y) ˄ ¬(Color(x) = Color( y))
D. ∀x, y Country(x) ˄ Country( y) ˄ Adjacent(x, y) => Color(x ≠y)
questions.correctAnswer: B. ∀x, y Country(x) ˄ Country( y) ˄ Adjacent(x, y) => ¬(Color(x) = Color( y))
questions.explanation: The sentence is a constraint: if two countries are adjacent, their colors differ. B uses implication correctly. A is equivalent but disjunctive form, C is conjunction without implication (requires all pairs to be adjacent and different, wrong), D has syntax error in Color(x ≠y).

questions.questionText: Among the given options choose correct one I. Von Neumann Architecture shares common memory for instructions and data. II. Harvard Architecture has separate memory for instruction and data
options: B. I and II are true
D. I and II are false
questions.correctAnswer: B. I and II are true
questions.explanation: The Von Neumann architecture uses a single shared memory space for both instructions and data, which can lead to the Von Neumann bottleneck. In contrast, the Harvard architecture employs separate memory spaces for instructions and data, allowing simultaneous access and potentially higher performance in certain applications.

questions.questionText: Suppose we want to compute the value y6, √y, y1/3 using the value of y. which of the following among Flynn’s CPU classification will be best suited for above calculation?
questions.explanation: SISD (Single Instruction Single Data) is suitable for scalar operations where a single instruction stream processes a single data stream sequentially. The computations like y^6, square root of y, and y^{1/3} are independent scalar operations on a single value y, fitting the SISD model.

questions.questionText: Vector and Array belongs to which class of Flynn’s classification.
questions.explanation: SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) is designed for parallel processing where the same instruction is applied to multiple data elements simultaneously, which is ideal for vector and array operations in applications like graphics processing or scientific simulations.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct statement(s) below: S1: CISC supports Fixed Length Instruction Format S2: RISC supports Variable Length Instruction Format S3: CISC supports Immediate Operand S4: RISC Allows only register operand
questions.explanation: RISC architectures typically use a load/store model where only load and store instructions access memory, and arithmetic operations are performed solely on registers. S1 is false because CISC often uses variable-length instructions, S2 is false because RISC uses fixed-length, and S3 is more characteristic of CISC.

questions.questionText: Assembly language
options: A. Uses alphabetic codes in place of binary numbers used in machine language
B. Is the easiest language to write programs
C. Need not be translated into machine language
questions.correctAnswer: A. Uses alphabetic codes in place of binary numbers used in machine language
questions.explanation: Assembly language uses mnemonic codes (alphabetic abbreviations) for instructions and symbolic names for addresses, making it more human-readable than binary machine code, but it still requires an assembler to translate it into machine language.

questions.questionText: In computers, subtraction is generally carried out by
questions.explanation: Most modern computers use 2's complement representation for signed integers because it simplifies arithmetic operations; subtraction can be performed as addition of the 2's complement of the subtrahend, and it handles negative numbers efficiently without separate signs.

questions.questionText: The amount of time required to read a block of data from a disk in to memory is composed of seek time, rotational latency, and transfer time. Rotational latency refers to
options: A. The time it takes for the platter to make a full rotation
B. The time it takes for the read-write head to move into position over the appropriate track
C. The time it takes for the platter to rotate the correct sector under the head
questions.correctAnswer: C. The time it takes for the platter to rotate the correct sector under the head
questions.explanation: Rotational latency is the delay waiting for the desired sector to rotate under the read/write head after the head is positioned over the correct track. On average, it's half the time for one full rotation of the disk.

questions.questionText: The circuite used to store one bit of data is known as
questions.explanation: A flip-flop is a basic memory element in digital circuits that can store a single bit of information (0 or 1) and maintain its state until changed by an input signal, forming the basis for registers and memory cells.

questions.questionText: The average time required to reach a storage location in memory and obtain its content is called
questions.explanation: Memory access time is the time interval between the initiation of a read/write operation and the availability of the data, including any addressing and decoding delays in RAM or cache.

questions.questionText: The idea of cache memory is based
options: A. On the property of locality of reference
C. On the fact that references generally tend to cluster
questions.explanation: Cache memory exploits locality of reference (temporal and spatial), the 90-10 rule (90% of time spent on 10% of code), and clustering of accesses to improve hit rates and reduce average memory access time.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is lowest in memory hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The memory hierarchy orders storage by speed and cost: registers (fastest), cache, RAM (main memory), and secondary memory (like HDD/SSD, slowest but largest capacity).

questions.questionText: Which of the following best characterize a computer that uses memory-mapped I/O?
options: A. the computer provides special Instruction for manipulating the I/O port
B. I/O ports are placed at addresses on bus and are accessed just like other memory location
C. to perform an I/O operation, it is sufficient to place the data in an address and call the channel to perform the operation
D. ports are reference only by memory-mapped Instruction of the computer and are located hard-wired memory location
questions.correctAnswer: B. I/O ports are placed at addresses on bus and are accessed just like other memory location
questions.explanation: In memory-mapped I/O, I/O devices are assigned addresses in the memory address space, allowing the CPU to access them using standard memory instructions, simplifying programming but potentially reducing available memory addresses.
