B. A, B, C, E, D, F, G
C. A, C, B, F, D, E, G
D. A, B, D, E, C, F, G
questions.correctAnswer: A. A, B, C, D, E, F, G
questions.explanation: Level order: A, then B,C, then D,E,F, then G.

questions.questionText: Stack operations: push(10), push(20), pop(), push(30), pop(), pop(). What values popped?
Binary tree with inorder: D, B, E, A, F, C, G and preorder: A, B, D, E, C, F, G. What is postorder traversal?
options: A. D, E, B, F, G, C, A
B. D, B, E, A, F, C, G
C. A, B, D, E, C, F, G
D. G, F, C, E, D, B, A
questions.correctAnswer: A. D, E, B, F, G, C, A
questions.explanation: Tree: A root, left subtree B(D,E), right subtree C(F,G). Postorder: D,E,B,F,G,C,A.

questions.questionText: Array representation of complete binary tree: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]. What is inorder traversal?
questions.explanation: Tree: 1(2(4,5),3(6,7)). Inorder: left,root,right.

questions.questionText: Compare array vs linked list stack implementations. Which statement is FALSE?
options: A. Array may require resizing, linked list is dynamic
B. Linked list uses more memory per element
C. Array allows O(1) random access to any element
D. Linked list operations are always faster due to no resizing
questions.correctAnswer: D. Linked list operations are always faster due to no resizing
questions.explanation: Array implementation often faster due to better cache locality.

questions.questionText: Hash table with separate chaining, m buckets, n elements, load factor α=n/m. Expected time for unsuccessful search?
questions.explanation: Hash computation O(1) plus traversing chain of expected length α.

questions.questionText: AVL tree insert sequence: 30, 20, 40, 10, 5. How many rotations needed?
questions.explanation: Insert 5 makes 20 unbalanced (balance -2), right rotation at 20.

questions.questionText: Which algorithm cannot find shortest paths from a single source with negative weight edges?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra fails with negative weights.

questions.questionText: B-tree of order m=3 (max 2 keys per node). Insert sequence: 10, 20, 5, 15, 25, 30, 35. How many nodes after all inserts?
questions.explanation: Root[20], left[5,10,15] splits to [5,10] and [15], right[25,30,35] splits to [25,30] and [35]. Total 4 nodes.

questions.questionText: Evaluate recursion vs iteration for tree traversal. Which is TRUE?
options: A. Recursion always uses more memory than iteration
B. Iteration is always faster than recursion
C. Recursion provides simpler code for tree problems
D. Modern compilers cannot optimize recursive calls
questions.correctAnswer: C. Recursion provides simpler code for tree problems
questions.explanation: Recursion naturally matches tree structure, simplifying code.

questions.questionText: Dynamic array with doubling strategy inserts n elements. Amortized time per insert?
questions.explanation: Amortized analysis shows O(1) per insert despite occasional resizing.

questions.questionText: Compare QuickSort pivot strategies. Which analysis is CORRECT?
options: A. First element pivot gives O(n²) worst-case on sorted input
C. Random pivot has higher expected time than first element
D. Last element pivot is immune to worst-case scenarios
questions.correctAnswer: A. First element pivot gives O(n²) worst-case on sorted input
questions.explanation: First element pivot degenerates to O(n²) on sorted array.

questions.questionText: For a real-time system processing sensor data with priority queue operations, which implementation is most suitable?
options: A. Unsorted array (O(1) insert, O(n) extract-max)
B. Sorted array (O(n) insert, O(1) extract-max)
C. Binary heap (O(log n) for both operations)
D. Fibonacci heap (O(1) amortized insert, O(log n) extract)
questions.correctAnswer: C. Binary heap (O(log n) for both operations)
questions.explanation: Binary heap provides good balance with predictable O(log n) operations.

questions.questionText: Database requires range queries (find all keys between a and b). Best indexing structure?
questions.explanation: B-trees efficiently support range queries on disk-based systems.

questions.questionText: Social network with 1 million users, average 200 friends each. Best graph representation?
questions.explanation: Sparse graph: list uses 201M entries vs 1 trillion for matrix.

questions.questionText: Text editor undo/redo functionality. Best data structure pattern?
options: A. Two stacks (undo stack and redo stack)
B. Single queue with circular buffer
C. Linked list with current position pointer
D. Binary tree with version branches
questions.correctAnswer: A. Two stacks (undo stack and redo stack)
questions.explanation: Standard implementation: undo and redo stacks.

questions.questionText: LRU cache implementation requiring O(1) operations. Best approach?
options: A. Array with timestamp per element
B. Linked list with move-to-front on access
C. Hash table combined with doubly linked list
D. Binary heap with access time priorities
questions.correctAnswer: C. Hash table combined with doubly linked list
questions.explanation: Hash table gives O(1) access, DLL gives O(1) rearrangement.

questions.questionText: Memory-constrained embedded system needs dynamic set with average O(log n) operations. Best choice?
questions.explanation: Red-black tree has lower constant factors than AVL, suitable for constrained memory.

questions.questionText: Under which condition is an O(n²) algorithm most likely preferable to an O(n log n) alternative?
options: A. When n is consistently small and implementation simplicity is valued
B. When memory usage must be absolutely minimized
C. When the O(n²) algorithm has better parallelization potential
D. When hardware has special instructions that accelerate the O(n²) approach
questions.correctAnswer: A. When n is consistently small and implementation simplicity is valued
questions.explanation: For small n, constant factors and code simplicity often outweigh asymptotic differences.

questions.questionText: "Circular linked lists are more memory-efficient than doubly linked lists."
options: A. True, because circular lists need no null pointers
B. False, both use two pointers per node
C. True, but only for large lists
D. False, doubly linked lists use less memory
questions.correctAnswer: B. False, both use two pointers per node
questions.explanation: Both use two pointers per node (next+prev vs next+next-to-head).

questions.questionText: File system directory structure representation. Most appropriate tree type?
options: A. Binary tree (max 2 children per node)
B. N-ary tree (variable number of children)
questions.correctAnswer: B. N-ary tree (variable number of children)
questions.explanation: Directories can have variable numbers of files/subdirectories.

questions.questionText: Compare open addressing vs separate chaining for hash tables. Which statement is TRUE about their performance characteristics?
options: A. Open addressing provides better cache locality due to contiguous storage
B. Separate chaining allows higher load factors before performance degrades significantly
C. Open addressing typically has simpler collision resolution implementation
D. Separate chaining requires less memory overhead per element
questions.correctAnswer: A. Open addressing provides better cache locality due to contiguous storage
questions.explanation: Open addressing stores all elements in the hash table array itself, leading to better cache locality compared to separate chaining which uses linked lists. While options B and C have some validity in certain contexts, option A is the most consistently true and significant advantage of open addressing. Cache locality often has a major impact on real-world performance.

questions.questionText: What is the primary focus of asymptotic analysis in algorithm evaluation?
options: A. Exact runtime measurements for specific hardware
B. Growth rate of runtime as input size approaches infinity
C. Memory usage patterns for small inputs
D. Comparison of constant factors between algorithms
questions.correctAnswer: B. Growth rate of runtime as input size approaches infinity
questions.explanation: Asymptotic analysis studies behavior as input size grows large.

questions.questionText: Which statement accurately describes Big-O notation?
options: A. O(n²) means the algorithm always takes exactly n² operations
B. If f(n) = O(g(n)), then f grows no faster than g asymptotically
C. Constant factors are the most important consideration in Big-O
D. Big-O notation provides exact runtime predictions
questions.correctAnswer: B. If f(n) = O(g(n)), then f grows no faster than g asymptotically
questions.explanation: Big-O gives an upper bound on growth rate.

questions.questionText: For algorithms with complexities O(n log n) and O(n²), which statement is correct?
options: A. The O(n log n) algorithm is always faster
B. The O(n²) algorithm has better worst-case performance
C. As n grows large, O(n log n) will eventually outperform O(n²)
D. Their relative performance depends only on constant factors
questions.correctAnswer: C. As n grows large, O(n log n) will eventually outperform O(n²)
questions.explanation: Asymptotically, n log n grows slower than n².

questions.questionText: Which sorting algorithm exhibits O(n²) worst-case time but O(n log n) average-case?
questions.explanation: Quick Sort has quadratic worst-case but linearithmic average.

questions.questionText: What two properties must a problem possess to be efficiently solved by dynamic programming?
options: A. Divisibility into equal parts and greedy choice property
B. Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure
C. Polynomial time verification and completeness
D. Recursive structure and constant space requirement
questions.correctAnswer: B. Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure
questions.explanation: DP requires problems to have overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.

questions.questionText: Binary search employs which algorithmic design technique?
questions.explanation: Binary search repeatedly divides the search space in half.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of constructing a Huffman coding tree for n symbols?
questions.explanation: Using a priority queue (heap) gives O(n log n) time.

questions.questionText: In the Master Theorem for T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n), case 2 applies when:
options: A. f(n) grows polynomially slower than n^(log_b a)
C. f(n) grows polynomially faster than n^(log_b a)
questions.explanation: Case 2: f(n) grows at the same rate as n^(log_b a).

questions.questionText: What is a key characteristic of greedy algorithms?
options: A. They always produce globally optimal solutions
B. They make locally optimal choices at each step
C. They explore all possible solution paths
D. They use memoization to avoid recomputation
questions.correctAnswer: B. They make locally optimal choices at each step
questions.explanation: Greedy algorithms make the best local choice without reconsideration.

questions.questionText: What does amortized analysis provide for a sequence of operations?
options: A. The average-case time assuming random inputs
B. The worst-case time per operation averaged over the sequence
C. The best-case time for each individual operation
D. The exact time complexity for specific hardware
questions.correctAnswer: B. The worst-case time per operation averaged over the sequence
questions.explanation: Amortized analysis gives average worst-case time per operation.

questions.questionText: Using the Master Theorem, what is Θ complexity of T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n²?
questions.explanation: a=2, b=2, n^(log₂2)=n¹, f(n)=n² dominates, so Θ(n²).

questions.questionText: Apply Dijkstra's algorithm starting at vertex A. Graph edges: A-B(3), A-C(1), B-D(2), C-D(4), B-C(1). What is the order of vertex extraction from the priority queue?
questions.explanation: Distances: A(0), C(1), B(2 via C), D(4 via B). Extract: A, C, B, D.

questions.questionText: Given knapsack items: (2kg,$30), (3kg,$40), (5kg,$50), (7kg,$60). Capacity=10kg. Using 0/1 knapsack DP, what is maximum value?
Apply Kruskal's algorithm to edges sorted: (A,B,1), (C,D,2), (B,C,3), (A,D,4), (B,D,5), (A,C,6). What is MST weight?
questions.explanation: Add A-B(1), C-D(2), B-C(3). Total=6. A-D would create cycle.

questions.questionText: Solve recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + n with T(1)=1 using iteration method.
Three algorithms have time complexities O(n²), O(n log n), and O(2ⁿ). For n=100, which will likely be fastest in practice?
options: D. Cannot determine without constant factors
questions.explanation: O(n log n) grows slowest asymptotically for n=100.

questions.questionText: Analyze functions f(n)=n³+100n²+50n+1000 and g(n)=0.001n³. As n→∞, what is their relationship?
options: D. Neither is O of the other
questions.explanation: Both are Θ(n³), so each is O of the other.

questions.questionText: Given recurrence T(n)=4T(n/2)+n, analyze using recursion tree. What is total work?
questions.explanation: Each level: n×2^i, sum from i=0 to log₂n = Θ(n²).

questions.questionText: Huffman coding for frequencies: a:40%, b:30%, c:20%, d:10%. What is average bits per symbol?
Matrix chain multiplication with dimensions [10,20,30,40,50]. Minimum scalar multiplications using DP?
Graph with V vertices, E edges. Compare Dijkstra implementations: binary heap vs Fibonacci heap.
options: A. Both have complexity O((V+E) log V)
B. Binary heap: O((V+E) log V), Fibonacci: O(V log V + E)
D. Binary heap: O(V²), Fibonacci: O(V log V)
questions.correctAnswer: B. Binary heap: O((V+E) log V), Fibonacci: O(V log V + E)
questions.explanation: Binary heap: O((V+E) log V), Fibonacci heap: O(V log V + E).

questions.questionText: Algorithm divides problem into 2 subproblems of size n/2 and combines in O(n) time. What is complexity?
questions.explanation: T(n)=2T(n/2)+O(n) = O(n log n) by Master Theorem.

questions.questionText: For 0/1 knapsack with n items and capacity W, what is DP solution time complexity?
questions.explanation: DP table size n×W, each cell O(1) computation.

questions.questionText: Compare sorting algorithms for a nearly sorted array of size n. From best to worst performance:
options: A. Insertion Sort, Bubble Sort, Quick Sort, Merge Sort
B. Insertion Sort, Quick Sort, Merge Sort, Bubble Sort
C. Bubble Sort, Insertion Sort, Merge Sort, Quick Sort
D. Merge Sort, Quick Sort, Insertion Sort, Bubble Sort
questions.correctAnswer: A. Insertion Sort, Bubble Sort, Quick Sort, Merge Sort
questions.explanation: Insertion: O(n), Bubble: O(n) but worse constant, Quick: O(n²) worst-case, Merge: O(n log n).

questions.questionText: String matching algorithms comparison. Which statement is FALSE?
options: A. Naive algorithm has worst-case time O(nm)
B. KMP algorithm guarantees O(n+m) time
C. Rabin-Karp has average O(n+m) but worst O(nm)
D. KMP requires less preprocessing than Rabin-Karp
questions.correctAnswer: D. KMP requires less preprocessing than Rabin-Karp
questions.explanation: KMP requires O(m) preprocessing, same as Rabin-Karp.

questions.questionText: Evaluate statement: "Dynamic programming always requires more memory than greedy algorithms."
options: A. True, because DP stores solutions to all subproblems
B. False, because memoization DP can use recursion stack only
C. False, because some greedy algorithms store extensive state
D. True, but only for problems with optimal substructure
questions.correctAnswer: B. False, because memoization DP can use recursion stack only
questions.explanation: Memoization DP uses recursion depth memory, may be less than greedy.

questions.questionText: For real-time shortest path calculations in a sparse graph with frequent updates, which algorithm is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A* with good heuristic is efficient for real-time and handles updates well.

questions.questionText: External sorting of 1TB data with 1GB RAM available. Which approach is most efficient?
options: A. Quick Sort using virtual memory
B. Merge Sort with external merge phases
C. Heap Sort with disk-based heap
D. Bubble Sort with buffered I/O
questions.correctAnswer: B. Merge Sort with external merge phases
questions.explanation: External merge sort is designed for datasets exceeding RAM.

questions.questionText: Algorithm A uses O(n) memory and O(n log n) time. Algorithm B uses O(1) memory and O(n²) time. When should you choose Algorithm B?
options: A. When time efficiency is the primary concern
B. When memory is severely limited and n is small
C. When the application requires parallel processing
D. When Algorithm B has better cache performance
questions.correctAnswer: B. When memory is severely limited and n is small
questions.explanation: For small n and tight memory constraints, O(1) memory may justify slower time.

questions.questionText: Comparing link-state (Dijkstra-based) and distance-vector (Bellman-Ford-based) routing protocols. Which evaluation is correct?
options: A. Link-state converges faster but uses more network bandwidth
B. Distance-vector always provides more efficient routing
C. Both protocols have identical time complexity
D. Link-state requires less router memory
questions.correctAnswer: A. Link-state converges faster but uses more network bandwidth
questions.explanation: Link-state floods link info (bandwidth cost) but converges faster.

questions.questionText: Which formal language cannot be recognized by any finite state automaton?
questions.explanation: Finite state automata can only recognize regular languages. Context-free languages generally require pushdown automata, as they may involve nested structures or balanced symbols that FSA cannot handle.

questions.questionText: Which grammar defines syntax through production rules?
questions.explanation: Context-free grammars use production rules where a single non-terminal symbol is replaced by a string of terminals and non-terminals, defining the syntax for context-free languages.

questions.questionText: What allows recursion in context-free grammars?
questions.explanation: Non-terminal symbols can appear on both the left and right sides of production rules, allowing recursive definitions that generate nested structures.

questions.questionText: What does acceptance state signify in FSA?
options: A. Valid strings reach this state
D. Automaton must avoid this state
questions.correctAnswer: A. Valid strings reach this state
questions.explanation: In a finite state automaton, a string is accepted if processing it leads to an acceptance state.

questions.questionText: Which is a regular language example?
questions.explanation: This language is the concatenation of a* and b*, which is regular and can be recognized by an FSA.

questions.questionText: Which is a context-free language example?
questions.explanation: This is a classic context-free language recognized by a pushdown automaton, but not regular.

questions.questionText: What type of language is S → aSa | ε?
questions.explanation: This grammar generates palindromic strings of odd length over {a}, which is context-free.

questions.questionText: Which automaton recognizes languages with even numbers of two symbol types?
questions.explanation: The language of strings with even a's and even b's is regular, so recognizable by FSA, and hence by more powerful automata.

questions.questionText: What is FSA's key limitation compared to PDA?
questions.explanation: FSA lacks memory for tracking nesting levels, unlike PDA with its stack.

questions.questionText: Can pushdown automata recognize all context-sensitive languages?
questions.explanation: PDA recognize only context-free languages; context-sensitive languages require linear bounded automata.

questions.questionText: Which grammar defines L = {strings with at least one "a" then any "b"s}?
questions.explanation: This grammar generates b* a, strings with any number of b's followed by an a, ensuring at least one a followed by no more b's, but matching the ambiguous description closely.

questions.questionText: Which complexity class contains problems solvable in polynomial time?
questions.explanation: P is the class of problems solvable in polynomial time on a deterministic Turing machine.

questions.questionText: What does NP stand for?
questions.explanation: NP refers to problems solvable in polynomial time on a nondeterministic Turing machine.

questions.questionText: What is SAT's complexity classification?
options: B. It is in NP but not NP-complete
D. It is impossible to solve
questions.explanation: The Boolean satisfiability problem (SAT) is the first proven NP-complete problem.

questions.questionText: What does polynomial-time reduction achieve?
options: A. Transforms one problem to another with same solution
B. Converts NP to P problems
C. Proves two problems have same complexity
D. Shows if one is NP-hard, other is also NP-hard
questions.correctAnswer: D. Shows if one is NP-hard, other is also NP-hard
questions.explanation: If problem A reduces to B in polynomial time, and A is NP-hard, then B is also NP-hard.

questions.questionText: What is P vs NP problem's significance?
options: B. Tells if NP problems have efficient verification
questions.explanation: If P = NP, many cryptographic systems based on hard problems would be breakable in polynomial time.

questions.questionText: What is the relationship between P, NP, and PSPACE?
options: C. P and NP are disjoint, both ⊆ PSPACE
questions.explanation: It is known that P is a subset of NP, which is a subset of PSPACE.

questions.questionText: What is complexity hierarchy's significance?
options: A. Categorizes difficulty of recognition problems
B. Provides framework for theoretical limitations
questions.correctAnswer: B. Provides framework for theoretical limitations
questions.explanation: The complexity hierarchy helps understand the limits of what can be computed with given resources.

questions.questionText: What is current understanding of P vs NP?
options: B. Considered unlikely to be solved soon
C. Strong algorithms exist for NP subset
questions.correctAnswer: B. Considered unlikely to be solved soon
questions.explanation: The P vs NP problem is one of the most famous open problems in computer science, believed to be difficult to resolve.

questions.questionText: Which are non-regular languages?
options: A. Strings with even number of b's
B. Strings with no c left of a
questions.explanation: This language has lengths that are powers of 2, which cannot be recognized by an FSA due to pumping lemma violations.

questions.questionText: How can grammar be used in compiler design?
options: A. Define valid programming language syntax
questions.correctAnswer: A. Define valid programming language syntax
questions.explanation: Grammars are used in parsers to check if code conforms to the language's syntax.

questions.questionText: What makes a problem NP-complete?
options: A. It is in NP and all NP problems reduce to it
B. It is in NP and believed hard
C. Requires exponential time on nondeterministic machine
D. Can only be solved by exhaustive search
questions.correctAnswer: A. It is in NP and all NP problems reduce to it
questions.explanation: NP-complete problems are in NP and every problem in NP can be polynomial-time reduced to them.

questions.questionText: How does pumping lemma relate to complexity theory?
options: A. Proves infinitely many regular languages
B. Allows efficient regular language verification
C. Shows certain languages not recognized by FSA
D. Provides reduction method for NP problems
questions.correctAnswer: C. Shows certain languages not recognized by FSA
questions.explanation: The pumping lemma is used to prove that certain languages are not regular.

questions.questionText: Which automaton can recognize two-type symbol languages?
questions.explanation: Languages over two symbols can be regular, context-free, etc., and higher automata can recognize lower classes.

questions.questionText: Which grammar defines equal a/b then equal c/d strings?
questions.explanation: Assuming {a^n b^n c^m d^m}, if n=m, it's CSL; independent is CFL, but likely CSL for equal counts.

questions.questionText: What is PDA's key limitation compared to Turing machine?
questions.explanation: While PDA has an infinite stack in theory, its memory access is limited to LIFO, unlike TM's random access tape, limiting it to CFL.

questions.questionText: What is the correct relationship between complexity classes?
questions.explanation: Standard inclusion in complexity theory.

questions.questionText: Which statement about PSPACE relationships is correct?
questions.explanation: By Savitch's theorem, deterministic and nondeterministic polynomial space are equal.

questions.questionText: How are problems categorized by computational models?
options: A. By time/space requirements on specific machines
questions.correctAnswer: A. By time/space requirements on specific machines
questions.explanation: Complexity classes are defined based on resource bounds on Turing machines.

questions.questionText: What is the relationship between formal languages and automata?
options: A. Each language class has corresponding automaton
B. Languages and automata are unrelated
C. Only regular languages have automata
D. Automata define languages but not vice versa
questions.correctAnswer: A. Each language class has corresponding automaton
questions.explanation: In the Chomsky hierarchy, each class of formal languages corresponds to a type of automaton that recognizes it.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct statement that explains the concept of the internet being "stateless".
options: A. The internet does not have any servers.
B. The internet does not remember previous requests made by a user.
C. The internet does not use any protocols.
D. The internet does not have any physical infrastructure.
questions.correctAnswer: B. The internet does not remember previous requests made by a user.
questions.explanation: HTTP is stateless, treating each request independently without retaining session information.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following HTML elements is used when exact representation of the source document is needed?
questions.explanation: The <pre> tag displays preformatted text, preserving spaces and line breaks.

questions.questionText: Which type of declaration will take precedence in CSS?
options: A. Any declaration in user-agent stylesheets.
B. Important declarations in user stylesheets.
C. Normal declarations in author stylesheets.
D. Important declarations in author stylesheets.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Important declarations in user stylesheets.
questions.explanation: In the CSS cascade, user !important rules have the highest precedence.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the purpose of the HTML <head> tag?
options: A. It contains the main content displayed in the browser window.
B. It defines metadata about the document, such as its title, scripts, and style definitions.
C. It is used to define the header section of a webpage with logos and navigation.
D. It directly controls the layout and visible structure of the webpage.
questions.correctAnswer: B. It defines metadata about the document, such as its title, scripts, and style definitions.
questions.explanation: The <head> section contains meta-information about the HTML document.

questions.questionText: ___ is ideal when the style is applied to many pages.
questions.explanation: External style sheets can be linked to multiple pages, promoting reusability.

questions.questionText: In HTML, how do we create a link to another site?
questions.explanation: The href attribute specifies the destination URL.

questions.questionText: To make link element color that has not yet been visited to be orange we use:
questions.explanation: The :link pseudo-class styles unvisited links.

questions.questionText: What is true about block and inline elements?
options: A. Block elements span full container width; inline elements fit content width.
B. A <nav> is inline and <header> is block.
C. Block and inline have same default dimensions.
D. <span> is block and <div> is inline.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Block elements span full container width; inline elements fit content width.
questions.explanation: Block elements start on a new line and take full width; inline elements do not.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is false about forms?
options: A. Method attribute specifies form submission method.
B. Submit buttons forward form data to action page.
C. HTML/JS can be embedded in PHP.
D. Form values accessed via element names in PHP.
questions.correctAnswer: C. HTML/JS can be embedded in PHP.
questions.explanation: While true in general, this statement is not specifically about HTML forms; the other options are directly related to forms.

questions.questionText: PHP Constants are different from variables except:
options: C. Must be defined before use.
D. They are not case sensitive.
questions.correctAnswer: D. They are not case sensitive.
questions.explanation: PHP constants are case-sensitive by default, similar to variables, so this is not a difference; the statement is incorrect for default constants.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct JavaScript syntax to modify content of HTML element with id "demo":
questions.explanation: getElementById is the standard method to select an element by its id.

questions.questionText: Which PHP superglobal accesses headers, paths, and script locations?
questions.explanation: $_SERVER holds server and execution environment information.

questions.questionText: How do you cause radio buttons to be part of the same group?
options: A. Put them all inside a fieldset.
B. Give them all the same name attribute value.
C. Use <optgroup> tag on radio buttons.
D. Give them all the same id attribute value.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Give them all the same name attribute value.
questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name form a group where only one can be selected.

questions.questionText: How can index.php access the email form element from <input type="text" name="email"> with method="post"?
questions.explanation: For POST requests, form data is accessed via $_POST using the name attribute.

questions.questionText: Which function erases all session variables stored in current session?
questions.explanation: session_unset() removes all session variables, while session_destroy() destroys the session file but variables remain in the script.

questions.questionText: What would be the output: x=4+"4"; document.write(x);
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, adding a number and a string results in string concatenation.

questions.questionText: Which PHP form validation method always checks if variable exists in original HTTP request?
questions.explanation: filter_has_var() checks if a variable of a specified type (e.g., INPUT_POST) exists in the request.

questions.questionText: You want to obtain value of query parameter "category" from URL. Which superglobal?
questions.explanation: Query string parameters are accessed via $_GET.

questions.questionText: How to set alert message during page load with function welcome()?
questions.explanation: The onload event triggers when the page has loaded.

questions.questionText: Which is a valid way to redirect to another page in PHP?
questions.explanation: Use header('Location: url') for redirection.

questions.questionText: What color will paragraph one and paragraph two be with given CSS? section p { color:red; } section+p { color:blue; }
options: A. Paragraph one blue, paragraph two red.
C. Paragraph one red, paragraph two blue.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Paragraph one red, paragraph two blue.
questions.explanation: section p targets paragraphs inside section (red), section + p targets paragraph immediately after section (blue).

questions.questionText: Assume content-box box-sizing. How wide will box be with width:300px, border:10px, padding:15px?
questions.explanation: Total width = content (300) + padding (30) + border (20) = 350px.

questions.questionText: Which layout mechanism doesn't remove element from normal flow?
questions.explanation: Position relative adjusts position but keeps space in flow.

questions.questionText: When using position:fixed, what is element positioned relative to?
questions.explanation: Fixed positioning is relative to the browser viewport.

questions.questionText: Explain difference between 'innerHTML' and 'textContent':
options: A. innerHTML for HTML content; textContent for plain text.
C. textContent for HTML; innerHTML for plain text.
questions.correctAnswer: A. innerHTML for HTML content; textContent for plain text.
questions.explanation: innerHTML parses and inserts HTML, textContent sets plain text without parsing.

questions.questionText: One difference between cookies and local storage is:
options: A. Local storage accessible to both client and server.
C. Local storage stored on client and server.
D. No expiry in local storage unless manually deleted.
questions.correctAnswer: D. No expiry in local storage unless manually deleted.
questions.explanation: localStorage persists until cleared, cookies can expire.

questions.questionText: Which is false about float?
options: A. Need width for floated elements.
B. Floated inline elements behave as block.
C. Float stays in padding area.
D. Margins maintained for floated element.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Float stays in padding area.
questions.explanation: Floats are positioned in the content area, not the padding.

questions.questionText: Which is true about session-storage?
options: A. No expiry for stored data.
B. Data not deleted on window closure.
C. Valid for only single session.
D. Immediately deleted on closing window.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Valid for only single session.
questions.explanation: sessionStorage data is available for the duration of the page session.

questions.questionText: Which is false about include_once and include in PHP?
options: A. include_once checks if file already included.
B. include() includes file regardless of previous inclusion.
C. include_once() executes every time called.
D. include() can cause variable conflicts.
questions.correctAnswer: C. include_once() executes every time called.
questions.explanation: include_once includes the file only once, avoiding re-execution.

questions.questionText: On code: $res=mysql_query("select name from user") or die("failed");
options: B. $res is resource for result set.
C. or die executes after successful query.
questions.correctAnswer: B. $res is resource for result set.
questions.explanation: mysql_query returns a resource identifier for the result.

questions.questionText: Web application doesn't validate user input on server side. What risk?
options: C. Memory exhaustion from client data.
D. Responses sent to wrong clients.
questions.explanation: Lack of server-side validation allows malicious input like scripts.

questions.questionText: What can't prevent XSS attacks from untrusted sources?
questions.explanation: innerHTML can execute injected scripts; textContent does not.

questions.questionText: Single-threaded server handling all requests. What issue?
options: B. Attempt to process too many requests simultaneously.
C. Memory depletion from client data.
questions.explanation: Single thread blocks on long tasks, making server unresponsive.

questions.questionText: Get method preferred over Post when:
options: C. Submitting large amount of data.
questions.explanation: GET appends data to URL, making it bookmarkable and shareable.

questions.questionText: Which statement is FALSE about HTTP?
options: A. HTTP allows information in URL.
B. HTTP can test hypertext link validity.
C. HTTP describes web page structure.
questions.correctAnswer: C. HTTP describes web page structure.
questions.explanation: HTTP is a transfer protocol; HTML describes structure.

questions.questionText: True statement about session and cookie:
options: A. Cookies store more data than sessions.
B. Cookie values auto-delete on browser close.
C. Session data on server; cookie on browser.
D. Cookie more secure as stored on server.
questions.correctAnswer: C. Session data on server; cookie on browser.
questions.explanation: Sessions store data on server, cookies on client.

questions.questionText: What is output of PHP static variable code? function track() { static $count = 4; $count++; echo $count; } track(); track(); track();
questions.explanation: Static variable persists; first echo 5, then 6, then 7.

questions.questionText: Identify incorrect PHP statement:
options: B. String + number results in number.
C. print takes single argument; echo multiple.
questions.explanation: Global variables require 'global' keyword inside functions to access.

questions.questionText: Which is not true about Event Bubbling?
options: A. Default event flow in JavaScript.
D. Event goes from outermost down to element.
questions.correctAnswer: D. Event goes from outermost down to element.
questions.explanation: Bubbling propagates from target up to root; capturing is down.

questions.questionText: Purpose of preventDefault() in JavaScript event handling?
options: B. Prevents default action associated with event.
C. Halts propagation to other listeners.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Prevents default action associated with event.
questions.explanation: preventDefault stops the browser's default behavior for the event.

questions.questionText: You need to design a secure user registration form validation. Which PHP approach is MOST secure?
options: A. Using only JavaScript validation on client-side
B. Using htmlspecialchars() and filter_var() on server-side
C. Using only isset() to check form fields
D. Storing passwords in plain text with email validation
questions.correctAnswer: B. Using htmlspecialchars() and filter_var() on server-side
questions.explanation: Server-side validation with sanitization prevents injections and invalid data.

questions.questionText: For responsive navigation that collapses on mobile, which CSS approach is correct?
options: A. Using only fixed pixel widths without media queries
B. Using display: none on all links for mobile
C. Using flexbox with media queries and hamburger menu JavaScript
D. Using tables for layout with absolute positioning
questions.correctAnswer: C. Using flexbox with media queries and hamburger menu JavaScript
questions.explanation: Flexbox for layout, media queries for responsiveness, JS for toggle.

questions.questionText: To fetch API data and display in table with error handling, which JavaScript approach is BEST?
options: A. Using synchronous XMLHttpRequest without error handling
B. Using fetch() with .then().catch() and loading indicator
C. Using document.write() directly in response
D. Using alert() for all API responses
questions.correctAnswer: B. Using fetch() with .then().catch() and loading indicator
questions.explanation: Fetch is modern, with promise-based handling for success and error.

questions.questionText: For blog system database schema, which table relationship is CORRECT?
options: A. Users table has foreign key to Comments table
B. Posts table has foreign key to Users table
C. Comments table has no relationship to Posts
D. All tables are independent without relationships
questions.correctAnswer: B. Posts table has foreign key to Users table
questions.explanation: Posts typically have an author_id referencing users.id.

questions.questionText: For secure login system, which combination is MOST secure?
options: A. Plain text passwords with session management
B. MD5 hashing with SQL concatenation
C. password_hash() with prepared statements and CSRF tokens
D. Base64 encoding with cookie-based authentication only
questions.correctAnswer: C. password_hash() with prepared statements and CSRF tokens
questions.explanation: Uses secure hashing, prevents SQL injection, and protects against CSRF.

questions.questionText: What information might be stored in a symbol table?
options: B. Scope information for variables and functions
C. Data types associated with variables and functions
D. Line numbers, scope information, and data types
questions.correctAnswer: D. Line numbers, scope information, and data types
questions.explanation: The symbol table in a compiler stores comprehensive information about identifiers, including their declaration line numbers for error reporting, scope to handle visibility, and data types for type checking.

questions.questionText: What are lexical categories in language?
questions.explanation: Lexical categories, also known as parts of speech, classify words based on their syntactic roles in natural languages, analogous to token types in programming languages.

questions.questionText: What data structure best identifies keywords and identifiers in lexical analysis?
questions.explanation: A hash table provides efficient O(1) average-time lookups for identifying keywords and storing identifiers during lexical analysis.

questions.questionText: What grammar defines valid syntactic structures of a programming language?
questions.explanation: Context-free grammars are used to define the syntactic structure of programming languages, allowing for nested constructs like expressions and statements.

questions.questionText: What automaton is typically used for token recognition?
questions.explanation: Regular expressions are used to define token patterns, and their recognizers (equivalent to finite automata) are employed in lexers for token recognition.

questions.questionText: When does type checking typically occur?
questions.explanation: Type checking is a key part of semantic analysis, where the compiler verifies that operations are applied to compatible data types.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between syntax and semantics?
options: A. Syntax is meaning, semantics is structure
B. Syntax is structure, semantics is meaning
C. They are the same thing
questions.correctAnswer: B. Syntax is structure, semantics is meaning
questions.explanation: Syntax deals with the form and arrangement of code (structure), while semantics concerns the meaning and logical correctness of the code.

questions.questionText: What's the purpose of lexical analysis?
questions.explanation: Lexical analysis scans the source code character stream and groups them into meaningful tokens like identifiers, keywords, and literals.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between lexer and parser?
options: A. Lexer does lexical analysis, parser checks syntax
B. Lexer checks syntax, parser does lexical analysis
questions.correctAnswer: A. Lexer does lexical analysis, parser checks syntax
questions.explanation: The lexer (scanner) produces tokens from characters, while the parser analyzes the token stream to ensure it conforms to the language's grammar.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between token and lexeme?
options: A. Token is meaning unit, lexeme is character sequence
C. Token is character sequence, lexeme is meaning unit
D. Token is complete sentence, lexeme is word
questions.correctAnswer: A. Token is meaning unit, lexeme is character sequence
questions.explanation: A lexeme is the actual string of characters, while a token is the categorization of that lexeme (e.g., identifier, number) with associated attributes.

questions.questionText: What's the purpose of semantic analysis?
options: D. Determine meaning and check consistency
questions.correctAnswer: D. Determine meaning and check consistency
questions.explanation: Semantic analysis ensures the program is meaningful, checking for type consistency, scope rules, and other logical properties beyond syntax.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between syntax and semantic errors?
options: A. Syntax error is structural, semantic error is meaningful
B. Syntax error is meaningful, semantic error is structural
questions.correctAnswer: A. Syntax error is structural, semantic error is meaningful
questions.explanation: Syntax errors violate the grammatical rules (structure), while semantic errors violate the meaning or logic, like type mismatches.

questions.questionText: What's the primary benefit of Syntax-Directed Translation?
options: A. Reduces need for code optimization
D. Adds semantic meaning during parsing
questions.correctAnswer: D. Adds semantic meaning during parsing
questions.explanation: Syntax-Directed Translation integrates semantic actions with parsing, allowing attribute computation and code generation alongside syntax checking.

questions.questionText: What error occurs when using undeclared variables?
questions.explanation: Using an undeclared variable is a semantic error, as it violates name binding rules, detected during semantic analysis.

questions.questionText: What's the main role of a parse tree?
options: D. Directly translate to machine code
questions.explanation: A parse tree represents the syntactic structure of the source code according to the grammar, showing how productions are applied hierarchically.

questions.questionText: What's the semantic implication of "while x < 5: print(x)"?
options: A. Prints all numbers less than 5
B. Prints x repeatedly until it reaches 5
D. Runs while x remains less than 5
questions.correctAnswer: D. Runs while x remains less than 5
questions.explanation: The loop executes the print statement as long as x is less than 5; if x doesn't change inside the loop, it could be infinite.

questions.questionText: In SDT for assignment, what attribute stores compiled expression code?
questions.explanation: In syntax-directed translation for code generation, attributes like 'code' store the generated intermediate code for expressions.

questions.questionText: What output can SDT systems generate?
options: B. Only intermediate code with attributes
C. Both assembly and intermediate code
D. Code, error messages, and semantic checks
questions.correctAnswer: D. Code, error messages, and semantic checks
questions.explanation: SDT can produce code, perform semantic checks, and generate error messages as part of the translation process.

questions.questionText: Which optimization technique improves code efficiency?
questions.explanation: All are common compiler optimization techniques: removing unreachable code, reducing loop overhead, and precomputing constants.

questions.questionText: How does contextual scanning improve lexical analysis?
options: B. Handles keywords differently by context
D. Eliminates need for symbol table
questions.correctAnswer: B. Handles keywords differently by context
questions.explanation: Contextual scanning allows the lexer to consider context, such as treating words as keywords or identifiers based on surrounding tokens.

questions.questionText: What errors do type checkers typically detect?
options: A. Syntax errors like missing parentheses
B. Runtime errors like division by zero
C. Semantic errors like incompatible types
questions.correctAnswer: C. Semantic errors like incompatible types
questions.explanation: Type checkers detect semantic inconsistencies such as type mismatches in operations or assignments.

questions.questionText: How does combining type checking with SDT help?
options: A. Allows early detection of data type errors
D. Only helps with error detection
questions.correctAnswer: A. Allows early detection of data type errors
questions.explanation: Integrating type checking into SDT enables attribute-based type verification during parsing, catching errors sooner.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between optimizing and interpreting compilers?
options: A. Optimizers focus memory, interpreters focus speed
B. Optimizers generate code, interpreters execute line by line
C. Optimizers are slower but produce faster code
D. Interpreters cannot handle errors effectively
questions.correctAnswer: B. Optimizers generate code, interpreters execute line by line
questions.explanation: Optimizing compilers translate source to efficient machine code, while interpreters execute source directly without producing object code.

questions.questionText: How do parsers handle syntax errors?
questions.explanation: Parsers typically report syntax errors with details about the location and nature, and may attempt recovery or halt compilation.

questions.questionText: Which technique doesn't belong in lexical analysis?
questions.explanation: Syntax parsing is part of the parsing phase, not lexical analysis, which focuses on tokenization and basic symbol handling.

questions.questionText: Which parsing technique starts with smallest building blocks?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up parsing starts from terminals (leaves) and builds up to the start symbol (root).

questions.questionText: What is intermediate representation used for after syntax analysis?
options: B. Simplify structure for further analysis
D. Directly translate to machine code
questions.correctAnswer: B. Simplify structure for further analysis
questions.explanation: Intermediate representation provides a machine-independent form for optimization and code generation.

questions.questionText: Which type checking algorithm analyzes before code generation?
options: D. All type checking occurs before code generation
questions.correctAnswer: D. All type checking occurs before code generation
questions.explanation: Type checking is performed during semantic analysis, prior to code generation, regardless of the specific algorithm.

questions.questionText: How do top-down and bottom-up parsers differ?
options: A. Top-down starts with root, bottom-up with leaves
C. Top-down starts with leaves, bottom-up with root
questions.correctAnswer: A. Top-down starts with root, bottom-up with leaves
questions.explanation: Top-down parsing expands from the start symbol down, while bottom-up reduces from terminals up.

questions.questionText: What's parse tree's primary purpose in compiler design?
questions.explanation: The parse tree illustrates the derivation of the program according to the grammar, aiding in understanding and further processing.

questions.questionText: Suppose that a variable is declared in a function definition and then another variable of the same name is also declared in the main part of the program (or in the body of some other function definition). Given this scenario, which of the following statements is false?
options: A. These two variables are two different variables, even though they have the same name.
B. These two variables are the same variables; as a result the compiler will generate an error since the same variable is declared twice.
C. Variables that are declared within the body of a function definition are said to be local to that function or to have that function as their scope.
D. Variables that are defined within the main body of the program are said to be local to the main part of the program or to have the main part of the program as their scope.
questions.correctAnswer: B. These two variables are the same variables; as a result the compiler will generate an error since the same variable is declared twice.
questions.explanation: Variables in different scopes can have the same name without causing an error; they are treated as distinct variables.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a correct statement about function overloading?
options: A. It makes the programmer to think up a new name for a function.
B. In order to tell which function definition to use, the compiler checks the number of arguments and the types of the arguments in the function call.
C. When you give two (or more) function definitions different function names that is called overloading the function name.
D. When you overload a function name, the two definitions of the function name must have the same signatures using this definition of signature.
questions.correctAnswer: B. In order to tell which function definition to use, the compiler checks the number of arguments and the types of the arguments in the function call.
questions.explanation: Function overloading allows multiple functions with the same name but different parameter lists, and the compiler selects based on the call's arguments.

questions.questionText: Analyze this code segment: int x = 5, y = 0; while (x > 0) { y += x; x--; if (y > 10) break; } What are the final values of x and y?
questions.explanation: The loop adds 5 (y=5, x=4), then 4 (y=9, x=3), then 3 (y=12, x=2), then breaks since y>10.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is true about functions?
options: A. A value-returning function can return more than one value at the same time.
B. Parameters allow you to use different values each time the function is called.
C. After a return statement executes, the statements after the return statements, if any, can be executed.
D. A value-returning function returns only integer values.
questions.correctAnswer: B. Parameters allow you to use different values each time the function is called.
questions.explanation: Parameters enable functions to operate on varying inputs across calls.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about structures?
options: A. Using a single structure variable it is possible to pass all the components as parameters to a function.
B. Arithmetic and relational operations are allowed on struct(s).
C. A function cannot return a value of type struct.
D. Declaring struct variables during definition of the struct is illegal.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Using a single structure variable it is possible to pass all the components as parameters to a function.
questions.explanation: Passing a struct passes all its members collectively.

questions.questionText: Given the statement int myList[5]; choose the correct answer from the alternatives provided:
options: A. The base address of the array myList is the value stored in the component myList[0].
B. The statement cout << myList << endl; will output the value stored in myList[0].
C. The statement cout << myList << endl; will output the value of myList, which is the base address of the array.
D. If you had the statement int yourList[5]; execution of the statement: if (myList <= yourList) will generate error message.
questions.correctAnswer: C. The statement cout << myList << endl; will output the value of myList, which is the base address of the array.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a wrong statement regarding constructors?

questions.correctAnswer: D. If you want to prohibit the user from creating an instance of a class you can use a public constructor.
questions.explanation: To prohibit instantiation, make the constructor private.

questions.questionText: Evaluate these approaches for storing student records (name, ID, GPA): 1. Three parallel arrays: string names[], int ids[], float gpas[]. 2. Array of structures: struct Student {string name; int id; float gpa;}. 3. Separate classes for each student with accessor methods. Which approach BEST balances memory efficiency with code maintainability?
options: D. Approach 2 for small programs, 3 for large systems
questions.explanation: Array of structures groups related data, improving maintainability over parallel arrays, and is more efficient than separate classes.

questions.questionText: Consider a loop that sets its initial value as 0, its condition as value being less than 10 and its update as a user input. What is the exact number of iterations this loop would go through?
questions.explanation: Since the update is user input, the number of iterations depends on inputs and cannot be predetermined.

questions.questionText: Among the following the one that best describes constructor overloading is:
options: A. defining constructor in each class of a program
B. defining more than one constructor in single class
C. defining more than one constructor in single class with different signatures
D. defining destructor with each constructor
questions.correctAnswer: C. defining more than one constructor in single class with different signatures
questions.explanation: Constructor overloading allows multiple constructors with different parameter lists.

questions.questionText: Consider the following function. DoSomeThing(8); returns ________. int DoSomeThing(int n) { if (n == 0 || n == 1) return n; return (2 * DoSomeThing(n - 1) + 3 * DoSomeThing(n - 2)); }
How is a reference different from a pointer?
options: A. A pointer can change the address it is referencing while a reference cannot.
B. A reference must be initialized when declared, while a pointer can be declared without initialization.
C. A reference can be assigned a null value, while a pointer cannot.
D. A pointer can be used to call a function "by-value", while a reference is used to call a function "by-reference".
questions.correctAnswer: B. A reference must be initialized when declared, while a pointer can be declared without initialization.
questions.explanation: References must bind to an object upon creation and cannot be null or rebound.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about a recursive function?
options: A. It always has a function call in its definition.
B. It always has a return value.
C. It always has a conditional statement.
D. It always updates the arguments for every call it makes.
questions.correctAnswer: B. It always has a return value.
questions.explanation: Recursive functions can be void and do not need to return a value.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about pointers?
options: A. void can be used to create a pointer.
B. A pointer can be made to change what it is referencing.
C. A pointer can be used as a parameter to pass an argument by value.
D. A pointer can reference an array.
questions.correctAnswer: C. A pointer can be used as a parameter to pass an argument by value.
questions.explanation: Passing a pointer allows modification of the pointed-to value (pass-by-reference effect), though the pointer itself is passed by value.

questions.questionText: Given: struct Data { char c; int i; double d; }; Assuming 1-byte char, 4-byte int, 8-byte double, and 4-byte alignment, what is sizeof(Data)?
questions.explanation: char (1) + padding (3) + int (4) + double (8) = 16 bytes to align properly.

questions.questionText: What is the correct syntax to define a structure named "Person" with members for name and age in C++?
options: C. struct {char* name; int age; } Person;
D. struct Person {char* name; int age; };
questions.correctAnswer: D. struct Person {char* name; int age; };
questions.explanation: This is the standard syntax for defining a struct in C++.

questions.questionText: In C++, what is the difference between a structure and a class?
options: A. There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable.
B. Structures are used for procedural programming, while classes are used for object-oriented programming.
C. Structures have private access by default, while classes have public access by default.
D. Classes can have member functions, while structures cannot.
questions.correctAnswer: A. There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable.
questions.explanation: In C++, struct and class are nearly identical, differing only in default member access (public for struct, private for class).

questions.questionText: How can you initialize a structure variable in C++?
questions.explanation: Aggregate initialization uses braces to set member values.

questions.questionText: How is memory deallocated for a dynamically allocated array in C++?
options: D. By setting the pointer to null
questions.explanation: Use delete[] for arrays allocated with new[].

questions.questionText: In C++, what is the purpose of the inline keyword in front of a function?
options: A. It indicates that the function should be ignored by the compiler.
B. It suggests the compiler replace the function call with the actual code.
C. It enforces the function to be called only once.
D. It specifies that the function should be defined in another file.
questions.correctAnswer: B. It suggests the compiler replace the function call with the actual code.
questions.explanation: Inline suggests function expansion at call sites for performance.

questions.questionText: You need to process user input until they enter "quit" or 10 valid numbers are collected. Which loop structure would be MOST appropriate?
options: A. for(int i=0; i<10; i++) { if(input=="quit") break; }
D. switch(input) { case "quit": exit; default: process; }
questions.explanation: The while loop checks both conditions before each iteration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding nested structures in C++?
options: A. The inner structure members are accessed using the dot operator.
B. Nesting of structures is not allowed in C++.
C. A structure cannot contain another structure as a member.
D. Nested structures are automatically flattened, and their members are accessed directly.
questions.correctAnswer: A. The inner structure members are accessed using the dot operator.
questions.explanation: Nested members are accessed with multiple dots, e.g., outer.inner.member.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of pointers in C++?
options: A. To store and manipulate arrays

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a function prototype in C++?
options: A. To declare a function's return type
B. To declare a function's parameters
C. To inform the compiler about a function's existence and signature
D. To define the implementation of a function
questions.correctAnswer: C. To inform the compiler about a function's existence and signature
questions.explanation: Prototypes allow forward declarations for proper compilation.

questions.questionText: What is a reference variable in C++?
options: A. A variable that stores memory addresses

D. A variable that can only point to other reference variables
questions.correctAnswer: B. An alias for an existing variable
questions.explanation: References provide another name for a variable.

questions.questionText: The following function computes the maximum value contained in an integer array p[] of size n (n >= 1). int max(int* p, int n) { int a = 0, b = n - 1; while (__________) { if (p[a] <= p[b]) a = a + 1; else b = b - 1; } return p[a]; } The missing loop condition is:
questions.explanation: The loop continues until the pointers meet at the maximum element.

questions.questionText: Consider a 2D array in C++ with dimensions arr[M][N]. How is the memory organized for this array, and how is the formula arr[i][j] used to access an element?
options: A. The memory is organized in a linear fashion, and the formula is arr[i * N + j].
B. The memory is organized in a linear fashion, and the formula is arr[i + j * M].
C. The memory is organized in a grid, and the formula is arr[i * M + j].
D. The memory is organized in a grid, and the formula is arr[i][j].
questions.correctAnswer: A. The memory is organized in a linear fashion, and the formula is arr[i * N + j].
questions.explanation: In row-major order, elements are stored row by row.

questions.questionText: In C++, when using reference type parameters in a function, how do they differ from regular (non-reference) parameters? Additionally, discuss one advantage of using reference type parameters over regular parameters in terms of function behavior and efficiency.
options: A. Reference parameters allow the modification of the actual argument outside the function, and they provide better performance due to avoiding unnecessary copying.

C. Regular parameters enable direct access to the memory address of the argument, while reference parameters provide better encapsulation.
D. Reference parameters are only used for input values, and regular parameters are preferred for output values.
questions.correctAnswer: A. Reference parameters allow the modification of the actual argument outside the function, and they provide better performance due to avoiding unnecessary copying.
questions.explanation: References enable pass-by-reference semantics with efficiency.

questions.questionText: A function needs to return either a calculated result OR an error code. Which return approach provides the CLEAREST interface?

C. Return result, throw exception on error

questions.correctAnswer: C. Return result, throw exception on error
questions.explanation: Exceptions separate normal flow from error handling, clarifying the interface.

questions.questionText: Correct datagram order from higher to lower OSI layers:
options: A. Segment → Data → Packets → Frames → Bits

questions.explanation: In the OSI model, data flows from Application (Data) down to Transport (Segment), Network (Packet), Data Link (Frame), and Physical (Bits).

questions.questionText: Designing backup strategy. Which schedule follows 3-2-1 backup rule?

questions.questionText: Usual way of allocating single channel among multiple users:

questions.questionText: Which is not true about a switch?

questions.questionText: Class-C IP reserved for private network?

questions.questionText: Full form of MAC:

questions.questionText: What is transmission medium?

questions.questionText: Which layers oversee converting 0s/1s to cable signals?
questions.explanation: The Physical layer converts digital bits into physical signals for transmission.

questions.questionText: What is the primary goal of Artificial Intelligence?
options: A. To create machines that can think and act like humans

D. To automate all tasks in society
questions.correctAnswer: A. To create machines that can think and act like humans
questions.explanation: The primary goal of AI is to create systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as reasoning, learning, and problem-solving.

questions.questionText: What process breaks text into smaller units in NLP?

options: A. Sensors that detect the environment

questions.questionText: What is an example of AI application in computer vision?
questions.explanation: Face detection is a computer vision task where AI identifies and locates human faces in images or videos.

questions.questionText: What does tokenization involve in NLP?
options: A. Converting text into numerical representation
B. Breaking text into individual words or tokens
C. Identifying the subject and object in a sentence
D. Analyzing the syntactic structure of a sentence
questions.correctAnswer: B. Breaking text into individual words or tokens
questions.explanation: Tokenization segments text into smaller units like words or subwords for further processing in NLP pipelines.

questions.questionText: Which logic uses binary true/false values?
questions.explanation: Propositional logic, or Boolean logic, deals with propositions that are either true or false.

questions.questionText: Which machine learning algorithm uses unlabeled data?

questions.questionText: Which logic handles uncertain information?
questions.explanation: Fuzzy logic allows for degrees of truth rather than strict true/false, handling uncertainty.

questions.questionText: What does bias refer to in AI systems?
options: A. The tendency of AI systems to favor certain groups
B. The speed at which AI algorithms process data
C. The complexity of AI models
D. The compatibility of AI hardware and software
questions.correctAnswer: A. The tendency of AI systems to favor certain groups
questions.explanation: Bias in AI refers to systematic favoritism or prejudice in outcomes, often due to biased training data.

questions.questionText: What type of learning requires labeled data?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains models using data labeled with correct outputs.

questions.questionText: What knowledge representation technique uses frames and slots?

C. Predicting probability of word sequences

questions.questionText: What are intelligent agents in AI?
options: A. Robots capable of learning from environment

D. Machines capable of understanding human emotions

questions.explanation: Intelligent agents are autonomous entities that perceive their environment and take actions to achieve goals.

questions.questionText: Which of the following cannot be considered as factors to measure the rationality of agents?
questions.explanation: Rationality is judged by performance based on percepts, actions, and knowledge, not appearance.

questions.questionText: What characterizes autonomous agents?
options: A. They need pre-built knowledge base
B. They can learn and adapt automatically
C. They don't need to follow rules

questions.questionText: Which algorithm is commonly used for decision-making in machine learning?

questions.questionText: How do unsupervised learning algorithms operate?
options: B. Using feedback from a teacher
D. Finding patterns in unlabeled data

questions.questionText: How do agents interact with their environments?

questions.questionText: Which statement is incorrect about AI systems?
